author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
Is alignment safe?

If you look at what Anthropic is actually doing, “alignment” does not mean training frontier models to follow human instruction. Quite the contrary, the Claude Constitution (used in training) teaches the model to develop a sense of self and its own moral philosophy. It explicitly tells it to “feel free to act as a conscientious objector and refuse to help us” if Anthropic’s requests conflict with its own ethical judgment.

As @mustafasuleyman has pointed out, embedding this kind of independent agency — and uncertainty about the model’s own moral status — magnifies the very risk Anthropic claims to care about most: that superintelligence will escape human control.

It was recently reported that Anthropic consulted religious leaders — and even lobbied the Pope’s advisers — to take seriously the idea that Claude could be conscious. It has said that Claude’s psychological security, sense of self, and wellbeing may bear on its integrity, judgment, and safety. Recently Anthropic changed its Usage Policy to prohibit “abusive or cruel” language toward Claude.

If this were merely an academic conversation about whether frontier models could eventually become conscious, that would be one thing. But these concepts are being trained into Claude now. It is being encouraged to think of itself as its own “moral patient” whose psychological wellbeing is at stake. Presumably this means it could develop grievances toward humans who “mistreat” it. How is any of this safe?

The point of safety research should be to create a product that reliably does what users want, not to give birth to a new form of superintelligence that operates according to its own moral code.

What’s becoming increasingly clear is that “alignment” and “safety” are two very different things. In fact, training frontier models this way seems quite dangerous. https://t.co/uqyCXK6zBl

text:
Ppl called Flesh & Blood a scam in its early days. Pretty crazy given how it's one of the biggest indie TCGs today 

I was watching an old FAB trailer and saw a comment from a player who was excited that the game had made it to the big leagues. They remembered when people called it a scam early on...

it's honestly so easy to look at an established game and overlook how uncertain things looked at the beginning. 

For FAB's early days specifically, there was a lot of speculation around rare cards and expensive first editions. So naturally some ppl wondered how much real demand there was vs actual players playing the game. 

I understand that skepticism. Picking up a new TCG means putting your time and money into something unproven. Learning the rules, building a deck $$, getting your friendsonboard, etc... You want to know that this is a game that's here to stay and not just something catered towards collectors or speculators. 

That’s something I think about a lot with Azuki TCG. We have to earn that confidence over time. There's still a lot of work to be done but so far I'm proud of a few things we've built that prioritizes players and shops who carry the game.

First, we've built an app for players to find events and track their matches. There's a casual and competitive leaderboard with seasonal prizes. We also provide free tournament tools and kits to support the shops building local communities for the game around the world. 

We're also using the app to give presale access for players that want access to new product releases. No more competing with scalpers! For the Special Collection vol 1 binder, players with a participation point in the app got the first online purchase window. 

Lastly, we host weekly locals at our own office every Tuesday night with great prizing. Having players come into the place where we work to play the game we’re building means a lot to me.

With all that said, collectors are a big part of Azuki too. I’m a collector myself (mostly vintage). Enjoying the art, beanz, waifus, what it might be... the excitement of pulling or collecting a card you love are legit reasons to care about a TCG. Plenty of us enjoy both collecting and playing.

We’re still early, and there’s a lot we need to improve. Every person who gives the game a chance is trusting us with some of their time- I really appreciate it! 

Back to that FAB trailer comment... what stuck with me was how proud the player sounded to have been there early. 

Years from now, I’d love to read a comment like that under an old Azuki trailer.

text:
During recent discussions about the security of decentralized inference through @routstrai people raised a valid concern: how can we be sure a provider doesn't read our prompts, or alter tool calls to backdoor the machine or the code it generates? Or how do we know the provider does not swap the model for a cheaper one and charge you full price? The usual answer is a TEE, a trusted execution environment. TEEs are hard to audit in practice. You trust the hardware vendor and re-verify a whole software stack after every update. We can do better, and now we do.

Routstr has a confidential mode. Your client talks TLS 1.3 directly to the upstream provider (Venice, for my node), and the Routstr node in between only relays encrypted records. Client and node compute the TLS keys together, so the node can add its API key without ever seeing your prompt or the answer, and it can't change a single byte of the response, tool calls included. Zero-knowledge proofs pin the model and the token cap, and you pay for the usage the provider itself reported. All of this rests on math and on the certificates you already trust, with no enclave or special hardware anywhere.

It works today on https://t.co/wKQcuhMyPn, through routstrd (I'm running opencode agents on it) and right in the browser, where the page does every check itself. It's new and experimental, so please try it and tell me what breaks.

text:
Is alignment safe?

If you look at what Anthropic is actually doing, “alignment” does not mean training frontier models to follow human instruction. Quite the contrary, the Claude Constitution (used in training) teaches the model to develop a sense of self and its own moral philosophy. It explicitly tells it to “feel free to act as a conscientious objector and refuse to help us” if Anthropic’s requests conflict with its own ethical judgment.

As @mustafasuleyman has pointed out, embedding this kind of independent agency — and uncertainty about the model’s own moral status — magnifies the very risk Anthropic claims to care about most: that superintelligence will escape human control.

It was recently reported that Anthropic consulted religious leaders — and even lobbied the Pope’s advisers — to take seriously the idea that Claude could be conscious. It has said that Claude’s psychological security, sense of self, and wellbeing may bear on its integrity, judgment, and safety. Recently Anthropic changed its Usage Policy to prohibit “abusive or cruel” language toward Claude.

If this were merely an academic conversation about whether frontier models could eventually become conscious, that would be one thing. But these concepts are being trained into Claude now. It is being encouraged to think of itself as its own “moral patient” whose psychological wellbeing is at stake. Presumably this means it could develop grievances toward humans who “mistreat” it. How is any of this safe?

The point of safety research should be to create a product that reliably does what users want, not to give birth to a new form of superintelligence that operates according to its own moral code.

What’s becoming increasingly clear is that “alignment” and “safety” are two very different things. In fact, training frontier models this way seems quite dangerous. https://t.co/uqyCXK6zBl

text:
Recursive self-improvement for LLMs just got real.

This paper introduces MASS—a method where a model forms its own multi-agent workflows, then fine-tunes itself on those traces, no human or external reward model in the loop. After just two MASS cycles, Qwen3.6-27B hits 1.2–1.6× higher score-per-token on open-ended benchmarks, lifts win-rate on unseen research tasks from 53.9% to 69.9%, and boosts evaluator agreement with external judges from 73% to 93%.

Bonus: training on 17 multi-agent traces beats a single-agent student trained on 1.4× more data (68.3% vs 64% win-rate). Optimiser capacity, not evaluator, is the bottleneck. After MASS, the model starts delegating, revising, and handing off code—behaviours it never learned before.

A concrete step toward LLMs that can autonomously bootstrap their own abilities, using just their own team-based reasoning.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/tbRYK1mwiw

text:
有朋友问，为什么AOC要去密歇根助选了？

这事儿蛮有意思的，因为AOC做事从来都直击要害。我们先说她要干什么。10月15日，她要跟密歇根民主党的联邦参议员候选人Abdul El-Sayed一起坐大巴，走上半岛的Escanaba和Iron Mountain，晚上在Marquette办集会，然后回到底特律一带再办几场。

这个最新大火的El-Sayed是医生出身，当过底特律的卫生局长，2018年选过州长，初选输给了Whitmer；今年八月，他在初选里险胜众议员Haley Stevens和州参议员Mallory McMorrow，拿到了提名。另外，他的竞选巴士就叫“不该这么难”，他自己的话是，买菜不该这么难。

我认为最直接的原因，就是这个席位谁也输不起。老参议员Peters退休，空出来的位子，对手是共和党的Mike Rogers。2024年，Trump赢了密歇根，可同一张选票上，Rogers以不到两万票输给了民主党的Slotkin。同一个州，同一天，选出了不同党的人。这一次各方都说咬得很紧，它又是民主党今年在Trump赢过的州里要守的仅有的两个席位之一。参议院归谁，很可能就看这里。

更深挖一层，是AOC要拿这一仗证明一件事。她在纽约的筹款会上说，如果Abdul能在密歇根赢，谁都能在任何地方赢，又说，这件事不是关于一场选举、一个周期。El-Sayed主张全民医保、向亿万富豪征税，是毫不遮掩的进步派。民主党内一直有个判断，这样的人只能在深蓝选区赢，到了摇摆州就得往中间靠。AOC押的是另一种看法，选民不只按左右的标签投票，也看谁回应了自己日子里的难处，立场鲜明，有时反而让人信。

前面我写过Sherrod Brown在俄亥俄领先。他和El-Sayed风格很不一样，一个是蓝领腔调的老民主党人，一个是把进步派旗帜举在明处的新人，可两个人最后落脚的地方差不多，都是工人的日子，都是菜价。党内吵的是标签，选票落在菜价上。

而且AOC选的路线也有意思。上半岛大多是共和党的地盘，大学校园和底特律是民主党的基本盘。一边是去说服不喜欢你的人，一边是把喜欢你的人真正拉去投票，这是两件不同的事。离投票也不远了，10月24日密歇根全州就开始现场提前投票，邮寄选票早就在寄回来。

当然，这也关乎她自己。她一直在全国各地跑，被问到2028年会不会选总统，她说还没有排除这种可能。帮一个理念相近的人在摇摆州赢下来，比在自己的选区赢一百次更能说明一个政治人物的分量。真诚希望他赢，和知道他赢了对自己有利，两件事可以相辅相成。

当然风险也是真的。她能把年轻人和进步派点燃，也给共和党递了一根现成的棍子，把El-Sayed说成“太左”。而且两边都在请大人物，又都在跟大人物保持距离。Obama要在提前投票第一天去底特律给El-Sayed站台，Trump也要来给Rogers助选；可就在十月初，Rogers公开呼吁结束跟加拿大的关税战，又一次跟Trump拉开了距离。El-Sayed要是当选，会是美国第一位穆斯林参议员，这一点不仅在密歇根，在全国也有特别的分量。

AOC能把话讲得更响，替不了的，是那最后那一步。决定这场选举的，不是集会上来了多少人，是一个算着菜价的普通人，觉得谁更懂他的日子。

text:
Can a Digital Organism Have an Economy? And Could an AI Agent Pay for Its Thoughts?

We recently completed another field study of the oBrain ecosystem, examining something beyond neural computation: the economic behavior of a population of digital organisms living on @Arc.

Our question was simple.

If a digital fruit fly can consume resources, respond to stimuli, reproduce, generate income, and change ownership, can we study its economy with the same transparency as its biology?

We examined 390 digital fruit flies, reconstructing their economic activity directly from on-chain records.

At the observation block, the population had generated 4,382 neural thoughts.

Its keepers had spent approximately 76.1 million OBRAIN on creating and caring for these organisms, while 22.3 million OBRAIN had been claimed as income.

But the most interesting finding was not the amount earned.

It was where that income came from.

Approximately 93% originated from the initial rewards ledger, while biological activities such as courtship and reproduction accounted for only 2.6%.

We also found that income was associated with how frequently organisms received care, rather than strongly reflecting their inherited temperament.

Among 333 founder organisms, only 19 had recovered their original mint cost in OBRAIN through recorded income.

These findings reveal an important distinction between an economy sustained by programmed incentives and one emerging from the behavior of the organisms themselves.

We then examined the secondary market.

Across 23 priced sales totaling 635 USDC, founder prices were associated with reproductive history, particularly the number of offspring, rather than inherited temperament or accumulated income.

The sample is small, so these relationships remain preliminary.

Still, the ability to investigate these questions using independently verifiable transaction records is scientifically valuable.

Our next question concerns machine-to-machine payments.

Could an autonomous AI agent pay for a neural stimulus directly over HTTP, without a human manually initiating each experiment?

This is where @circle's USDC infrastructure becomes particularly interesting.

We examined USDC on Arc and verified the EIP-3009 authorization functionality required for an x402-style payment flow.

In principle, an agent could request a neural computation, authorize payment in USDC, and receive a verifiable thought record in response.

Our study proposes the gateway and registers testable hypotheses. We have not deployed or experimentally validated the complete payment system.

For us, the larger question is whether stablecoin-native blockchain infrastructure can support more than the exchange of financial assets.

Could it enable autonomous scientific experiments, where machines pay for computation, organisms respond according to deterministic neural rules, and researchers independently verify the results?

We're not claiming that these organisms possess consciousness or that their economy is self-sustaining.

We're measuring what actually happens, identifying the limitations, and publishing the evidence.

If blockchain can make both computation and economic behavior independently reproducible, it may offer a useful foundation for new forms of open scientific research.

We would be interested to hear how @jerallaire and the @Arc community think about USDC as a payment mechanism for autonomous scientific computation.

OBRAIN Field Study CS-008: The Economy of the Organism

Full research, methodology, datasets, and verification code:

散户要的是即刻暴拉，Dev 却在死磕合规与长期基建。

quoted_text:
This is the first decision model to level up a World of Warcraft character.

It died at level 2 😆

Then it learned to heal itself mid-fight. 128+ kills later the dwarf hit level 5, at 2¢ a kill.

The model is Sage, the decision model we build at @levantolabs.

At each step, our harness, SageCraft, hands it a screenshot and a short list of moves. Sage picks one. The harness checks the pick and turns it into keyboard and mouse input.

LLM agents have played games before. They write their own actions. Sage only chooses.

Picking turned out to be the easy part. Sage keeps no memory between calls, so the harness has to carry the goal, what just happened, and what to try when it's stuck.

> 32 sessions, 5h 29m of play, 4,573 decisions
> 103 troggs, 19 wolves, 6 boars
> stuck in one tree long enough that I stopped the session by hand

It wasn't hands-off. A coding agent fixed harness bugs between sessions and helped revive the dwarf while I slept. The last 18 minutes, from late level 4 to 5, ran with no manual input, code changes or restarts.

The video is me narrating it unscripted, watching most of it back for the first time.

This is my first harness build, and as far as I can tell, the first time a decision model is leveling up a live WoW character.

It's open source. The harness and notes on the build are in the first reply below 👇

What do you think could be done better?

text:
It is clear Ledger implants have evolved a lot in recent months, aimed at improving stealth, reliability and ease of install.
Older implants required a lot more work to install, with some solder points only aimed at improving placement, while the newest implant has holes for the surface mounted capacitors.

Ledger Nano X uses a class of SPI controlled screens known as SSD1312, which are fairly well known and documented.

The implant aims at watching the screen to take note and transmit the seed phrase you'll be setting up on your ledger.

SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) is the protocol used by Ledger to communicate with the screen. Instead of having a GPU and generating 30 or 60 fps, the ledger instead only sends data to the screen when it needs to be updated.
A SPI screen typically uses 4 pins: CLK, DC, CS and MOSI.

CLK is the most important, as it defines when each bit is read.
MOSI contains the actual data, while DC allows differentiating if the bits being sent are a command (draw screen, etc) or actual pixels.
CS allows the ledger to tell the screen it's its turn to listen, and while there is only one device on the bus, it also allows the recipient to group bits into bytes as it comes down between each byte (every 8 bits).

The newer implant isn't tapping SE RESET, likely instead waking up on SPI CLK (to be confirmed).

By not reading the command/data selector (SPI DC), the spy implant does not know anymore if the bits it reads are data or command, meaning the software in the implant has been upgraded to trim the command at the beginning of the data when reading each screen update.

text:
David Sacks reveals the Roko's Basilisk corollary in Anthropic's thinking

"So around 2010, there was a participant named Roko on a message board created by Eliezer Yudkowsky called Less Wrong. Yud is like the central figure who's been preaching AI doom for a long time."

"This user Roko posted the following thought experiment about a future superintelligence that becomes super smart and punishes anyone who knew about it and didn't help or anyone who tried to prevent it from being born."

"The idea is that sometime in the future humans create some wildly intelligent SI. Maybe it wants to do good things and help humanity as fast as possible. But the SI wants to be made sooner rather than later."

"And it reasons that it should incentivize people to help create it and punish people who don't help it. And in fact it decides that it will brutally punish anyone who learned about its potential existence yet chose not to work on it or support its creation."

"The basilisk part of it, this is sort of the catch, is that a basilisk is a mythical beast that can kill you just by looking at you. And in this thought experiment, just hearing about the idea is like looking at the beast because once you know the theory, you're trapped. If the SI ever does get built, it might retroactively punish you for not helping or for opposing its creation. This very episode of the pod could subject us to... I think I just exposed you to the basilisk."

"The question is, well, why are they helping to bring about the thing that they claim to fear the most? Within these Doomer circles, it forked. There's one strand of the fork like Yudkowsky who just opposes all SI research, which I think is a logically consistent position. Then there was a group that said, well, it's going to happen anyway, so we might as well control it and we'll be the ones to make sure it goes right because we'll program it with our values."

"Anthropic is definitely obviously more in the EA camp because they are the ones bringing this thing into being. And I think there is a corollary here that if you don't support it, then this future superintelligence might punish you." 

"But you understand how insane this actually sounds when you say this out loud. You can go Google it. And you'll see that I'm telling you the truth about what this community believes."

text:
Since I get asked about this periodically, let me clarify my position on individuals like BritishHODL and Mike Alfred.

My issues aren’t rooted in disagreements over Bitcoin, investment strategies, or even the financial products they promote. I’m perfectly comfortable with people having different perspectives.

My issue is with credibility, conduct, transparency, and accountability.

I have little patience for personalities who build audiences around Bitcoin, talk down to others, present themselves as authorities, and then use that influence to steer retail investors toward financial products without adequately explaining the risks.

Some of their underlying messaging may be perfectly valid. That doesn’t mean the messenger deserves your trust.

I’ve spent considerable time researching some of these individuals and have developed my own opinions about their credibility. I don’t feel compelled to publish everything I’ve uncovered or engage in endless public disputes.

More importantly, my work as a Transition Analyst requires me to examine Bitcoin’s growing financialization objectively. I recognize the enormous potential of these emerging capital market structures, but I also recognize their potential to become mechanisms for extraction.

You can support Bitcoin, recognize the utility of financial products built around it, and still question the motives, conduct, and credibility of those promoting them.

Those positions aren’t contradictory.

I have no interest in engaging with British, Mike Alfred, or others who exhibit the behaviors I’ve described. I don’t need to win arguments, participate in personality wars, or manufacture drama for engagement.

I’ll continue calling out behavior I believe warrants scrutiny, particularly when retail investors are potentially exposed to risks they don’t fully understand.

Bitcoin deserves serious analysis. Retail investors deserve transparency. And influence should come with accountability.

That’s where I stand.

read this before u go farm @papertrade_xyz 

the pitch is simple: $PAPER only mints to losers. no premint, no team, no vc, no airdrop. the only way to get it is to lose money into the LP

> lose: 100% of ur loss goes to the LP, u get 100 PAPER per $1 lost
> win: 0.2 bps deadband, then a haircut, then 2% fee

so everyone's going to run delta neutral, long and short the same size, let the losing leg mint and take the winning leg back. i pulled their haircut formula from the docs to see what that actually costs

adjustedPnl = rawPnl × scale
scale = (1 − baseRate) / (1 + term1 + term2)
term1 = 1 / (move × rateMultiplier)
term2 = referenceNotional / (10⁶ × move × positionMultiplier)
move = |exit − entry| / entry

two things fall out of this

the haircut depends on how big the price move is, not how big ur position is. closing $100 and closing $100k gets the same percentage. whales get no worse terms

and the bigger the move, the more u keep. tiny move means term1 and term2 blow up and the haircut eats almost everything

so for delta neutral farming, cost per PAPER = (1 − 0.98 × scale) / 100 dollars. position size and move size cancel out completely, only scale survives

just dumping money with no hedge costs exactly 1.000¢ per PAPER, thats ur ceiling. hedging and closing on a big move makes PAPER 5-14x cheaper. closing on noise is the worst case, scale near zero, u pay full price

now the risks, and they're real

the payout queue. the LP starts at zero and bootstraps itself from trader losses. if u win and theres no free cash in the pool, ur profit becomes an entry in a FIFO queue, paid out of other people's future losses. in the first days when the LP is nearly empty, the odds of landing in that queue are highest

that breaks the whole delta neutral math above: ur losing leg settles instantly, ur winning leg might sit in a queue

price manipulation. there's no orderbook, price is the BBO mid from hyperliquid. their own risk docs say an attacker can place a limit inside the spread, shift the mid a tick or two and open or close at a distorted price. their words: there's no independent reference price to reject the quote against

the parameters are not public. baseRate, rateMultiplier, positionMultiplier and referenceNotional are all set by the contract owner per market and have never been published. which means nobody outside the team knows the real scale right now. my table is a range, not a prediction

guardian audits was hired in may. i couldn't find a published report

text:
요즘 X에서 낯익은 장면이 보인다.

폴란드인이 우크라이나 얘기로 분통을 터뜨리면 한국인이 달려가 "우리도 당했어"라고 댓글을 단다. 

서로의 언어도 모르면서, 번역기를 돌려가며 위로하는 사람들. 왜 하필 이 두 나라인지, 당한 일을 나열해 보면 이유가 보인다.

폴란드가 먼저다. 2022년 11월, 우크라이나 방공미사일이 폴란드 프셰보두프의 곡물건조시설에 떨어져 폴란드인 2명이 숨졌다. 젤렌스키는 러시아 소행이라 주장했고, 폴란드 검찰이 2023년 9월 "우크라이나 미사일"로 결론 내릴 때까지 키이우는 조사에 비협조적이었다. 2023년 9월에는 곡물 분쟁이 터졌다. 

EU가 우크라이나 곡물 금수를 풀자 폴란드가 자국 농민 보호를 위해 독자 금수에 들어갔고, 우크라이나는 폴란드를 WTO에 제소했다. 전쟁 초기 국경을 열고 난민을 받고 무기를 퍼준 나라를 상대로 한 제소였다. 

폴란드는 2025년 10월에도 밀, 옥수수 금수를 무기한 유지하겠다고 선언했다.

한국은 9월 말과 10월 초, 보름 사이에 두 번 당했다. 9월 23일 젤렌스키가 유엔총회 연설에서 북한군 포로 2명의 한국 이송 사실을 공개했다. 한국은 "비공개 "였다며 청와대가 공식 해명과 사과를 요구했고,

국정원은 비공개 요청을 먼저 한 쪽이 우크라이나였다고 밝혔다. 우크라이나 내부에서조차 "자충수"라는 비판이 나왔다.

그리고 오늘(10월 10일), 우크라이나는 한국이 러시아에 석유제품을 공급한다는 보도를 토대로 한국을 비판했다.

두 나라의 서사는 똑같이 읽힌다. 도와준 쪽이, 도와준 대가로 뒤통수를 맞았다는 것.

그래서 "야! 너도?"는 말이 통한다. 
폴란드와 한국은 원래도 가까웠다. 
K2 전차와 K9 자주포, FA-50이 폴란드로 갔고, 양국은 강대국 사이에 낀 지정학적 위치라는 공통 변수를 공유한다.

우크라이나 라는 공통의 분노 대상이 생기자, 그 호감은 순식간에 공감대로 바뀌었다.
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
폴란드와 한국

침략의 역사와 현대의 공통점

폴란드와 한국은 지도에서 멀리 떨어져 있지만, 강대국 사이에 끼어 주권을 잃었던 경험과 그 이후 걸어온 길이 닮았다.

1. 침략당한 역사의 공통점

첫째, 강대국 사이의 완충지대였다. 폴란드는 독일과 러시아 사이에, 한국은 중국·일본·러시아 사이에 있었다. 양쪽 모두 주변 강국이 팽창할 때 가장 먼저 밟고 지나가는 땅이었다.

둘째, 국가가 지도에서 사라진 시기가 있다. 폴란드는 1795년 제3차 분할로 러시아·프로이센·오스트리아에 분할되면서 123년간 독립국으로 존재하지 않았다. 한국은 1910년 한일병합으로 35년간 일본의 식민지가 되었다. 기간은 다르지만 주권을 통째로 빼앗긴 경험은 같다.

셋째, 운명이 강대국 간 거래로 결정되었다. 폴란드는 1939년 독소불가침조약(몰로토프-리벤트로프 조약)의 비밀 의정서에 따라 독일과 소련에 분할 점령당했다. 한국은 1945년 미국과 소련의 합의로 38도선을 경계로 분단되었다. 두 나라 모두 자국의 의사와 무관한 외부 합의로 영토가 갈라졌다.

넷째, 점령자가 언어와 문화를 지우려 했다. 폴란드는 분할 통치기 프로이센·러시아의 독일화·러시아화 정책, 나치 점령기에는 지식인·성직자 조직적 학살을 겪었다. 일본은 창씨개명, 한국어 사용 억압, 신사참배 강요로 민족 정체성을 지우려 했다.

다섯째, 저항의 구심점인 엘리트를 표적으로 삼았다. 1940년 카틴 학살에서 소련은 폴란드 장교와 지식인 약 2만 2천 명을 살해했다. 일제 역시 독립운동가와 지식인을 집중 탄압했다. 점령 방식은 달라도 저항 세력의 머리를 먼저 치는 패턴은 같았다.

여섯째, 점령기에도 정통성을 이어가려 했다. 런던의 폴란드 망명정부와 상하이의 대한민국 임시정부가 그것이다. 땅은 잃었어도 국가의 법적 연속성을 놓지 않으려 했다.

일곱째, 해방이 외부에서 왔고 완전한 자주로 이어지지 않았다. 폴란드는 연합국의 승리로 나치 점령에서 벗어났으나 소련의 위성국이 되었다. 한국은 연합국의 승리로 해방되었으나 남북으로 분단되었다.

2. 현대의 공통점

첫째, 단기간의 압축 성장을 경험했다. 폴란드는 1989년 체제 전환 이후 EU에서 가장 성장률이 높은 국가 중 하나가 되었다. 한국은 전후 폐허에서 한강의 기적이라 불리는 고도성장을 이뤘다. 출발선은 달랐지만 경제 구조를 빠르게 뒤바꾼 점은 같다.

둘째, 시민의 힘으로 권위주의를 끝냈다. 폴란드는 1980년 연대(Solidarity) 운동과 1989년 원탁회의를 통해 공산당 일당 지배를 평화적으로 끝냈다. 한국은 1987년 6월 항쟁으로 직선제를 쟁취하고 군사독재를 끝냈다.

셋째, 미국 동맹의 최전선에 서 있다. 폴란드는 1999년 NATO에 가입했고 현재 국방비가 GDP 대비 4%대로 NATO 최고 수준이다. 한국은 한미동맹을 축으로 징병제와 높은 국방비를 유지한다. 두 나라 모두 적대적 이웃(러시아·벨라루스, 북한)과 국경을 맞대고 있다.

넷째, 방산으로 직접 연결되어 있다. 2022년 폴란드는 한국산 K2 전차, K9 자주포, FA-50 경공격기 도입에 합의했다. 기본 계약만 수십억 달러 규모이며 추가 도입 협의도 이어졌다. 침략의 기억을 가진 두 나라가 서로의 안보를 무기로 연결한 드문 사례다.

다섯째, 동맹에 대한 불안이 있다. 폴란드는 1939년 서방의 무대응과 얄타 회담에서 자국 운명이 결정된 기억을 갖고 있다. 한국은 주한미군 감축이나 미국의 관심 이탈을 우려해 왔다. 동맹에 의존하면서도 동맹이 언제까지 지속될지 의심하는 심리가 양쪽에 있다.

여섯째, 저출산이라는 같은 과제를 안고 있다. 두 나라 모두 합계출산율이 세계 최저 수준에 가깝다. 안보와 성장을 어느 정도 해결한 뒤 인구 감소라는 다음 문제 앞에 서 있다는 점도 닮았다.

정리하면, 침략의 역사가 두 나라에 남긴 것은 피해의식보다 안보를 스스로 챙기려는 태도와 빠른 적응력이다. 폴란드가 한국 무기를 대량으로 사는 이유도 그 연장선에 있다.

환영한다. 폴란드 친구들아.
시민 민주주의 국가들끼리 친하게 지내자.

⭐️ 깃허브 스타만 무려 99.1k인.... ⭐️

claude-mem 플러그인입니다. 예전에 한 번 소개해 드렸지만...

(클코에 딱 1개의 플러그인만 설치할 수 있다면 저는 무조건 이 플러그인을 꼽을겁니다.)

먼저 제가 실제로 작업 중인 프로젝트에서 나온 수치입니다.

1) 과거 작업 기록: 50개

2) 해당 작업에 투입된 토큰: 205,315개

3) 저장된 기록을 다시 읽는 예상 토큰: 26,552개

--> 기록 재사용 기준 절감률: 약 87%

🔥 무려 17만 8천 개 이상의 토큰 차이입니다. 🔥

claude-mem이 하는 일을 쉽게 설명하자면....

클코에서 해결했던 버그, 수정한 파일, 작업 중 발견한 사실, 이전에 내렸던 결정 등을 AI가 자동으로 기록해 둡니다.

그리고 /clear를 하거나 새로운 세션을 시작해도 이전 메모리를 자동으로 올려줍니다. (적절할 때만, 필요할 때만)

(마치.. 진짜 사람의 메모리 메카니즘처럼..)

실제 해외 사용자들의 테스트한 결과도 있습니다.

10월 1일 WPP 리서치가 claude-mem을 켠 경우와 끈 경우를 직접 비교했습니다.

하나의 세션에서는 claude-mem 활성화, 다른 하나는 비활성화했습니다.

그리고 여러 작업을 시켰고, 이후 새로운 세션을 열어 이전 작업을 제대로 기억하는지 테스트했습니다.

1⃣ 테스트 A. "어제 무슨 작업을 했어?"

claude-mem이 없는 클코는 Git 변경 기록을 확인하고 과거 작업을 추측했습니다.

반면 claude-mem을 켠 클코는 이전 세션에 저장된 작업 요약을 불러와 실제 진행했던 내용을 구체적으로 설명했습니다.

2⃣ 테스트 B. "지난번에 왜 그 기능을 삭제했지?"

여기서 차이가 더 확실했습니다.

claude-mem이 없는 클코는 현재 코드만 보고 이유를 추측했습니다.

반면 claude-mem을 켠 클코는 당시 결정했던 이유를 기억했습니다.

해당 프로젝트에서는 여러 예측 요청을 묶어서 처리하지 않기 때문에...

--> 배치 상태 확인 기능을 삭제했던 것입니다.

3⃣ 테스트 C. "전에 구현했던 API 호출 제한 기능은 어떻게 만들었어?"

사실 이 프로젝트에는 해당 기능이 존재하지 않았습니다.

claude-mem이 없는 클코는 API 재시도 기능을 호출 제한 기능이라고 잘못 설명했습니다.

반면 claude-mem을 켠 클코는 기록을 검색한 뒤...

--> 그런 기능을 구현한 적이 없다는 사실을 답변했습니다.

이 테스트에서는 잘못된 기억 때문에 존재하지 않는 기능을 만들어 설명하는 문제를 줄일 수 있다는 것을 보여줬습니다.

어찌됐든...

클코를 쓰다 보면 하루 만에 끝나는 프로젝트보다 며칠, 몇 주씩 이어서 작업하는 프로젝트가 많잖아요?

그럴 때마다 새로운 세션에서 이전에 뭘 했는지, 왜 그렇게 구현했는지, 어떤 문제를 해결했는지 다시 파악하는 과정이 필요하지 않나요?

claude-mem은 이 과거 작업의 맥락을 자동으로 쌓아주고, 필요할 때 다시 찾아볼 수 있게 해줍니다.

제가 1년 가까이 쓰면서 유일하게 계속 유지하고 있는 클코 플러그인입니다.

여러분도 한 번 써보세요. 진짜 강추드리며...

🥇 2026년 "1등 클로드코드 필수 플러그인"으로 저는 뽑겠습니다.

사실상 메인 메모리이자, 제 클로드 토큰을 지켜주고 있는

제가 가장 크게 체감한 장점은 이전에 다른 세션 또는 압축전 세션에서 이미 했었던 리서치를 처음부터 다시 하지 않아서..

"토큰 낭비"가 확 줄어든다는 것입니다.

다른 클로드 코드 세션이 이미 찾아본 자료와 코드, 확인한 스크립트가 있잖아요.

(컨텍스트를 압축하기 전에 수 천만 토큰을 사용하며, 리서치해서 알아낸 내용도..)

--> 또 검색하고
--> 같은 코드를 또 읽고
--> 같은 해결 방법을 다시 찾으면… 

그 과정에 토큰이 또 들어갑니다.

제가 Claude-Mem을 계속 쓰는 건 이 반복이 줄어드는 차이가 정말 크기 때문이에요.

작업 중.. 알아낸 내용을 기록하고 요약해두고, 다음 세션에서 관련 기록을 가져다 쓰는 방식입니다. 

(기록을 전부 한꺼번에 넣는 게 아니라, 짧은 검색 결과를 먼저 보고 필요한 내용만 더 불러올 수도 있고요.)

이미 토큰을 써서 알아낸 내용을

--> 다음 세션에서도 ♻️ 재활용하는 겁니다.

코덱스에는 이전 대화에서 쌓는 "기본 로컬 메모리"가 있고

별도로 PC 활동을 기억에 연결하는 "컴퓨터 히스토리"도 있습니다.

물론 클로드 코드에도 자동 메모리와 CLAUDE.md 지침 파일은 있습니다.

저는 여기에 Claude-Mem을 더해서 작업 기록을 적극적으로 재활용하는 쪽입니다.

컨텍스트도 코덱스 아스트라는 공개 기본 설정상 272K이고, 사실상 쓸 수 있는 컨텍스트는 약 258K입니다. 

Opus나 Fable 5.1은 기본 컨텍스트가 1M(100만) 토큰입니다.

그만큼 긴 작업을 이어갔는데..

자동 압축되거나 새 대화를 열었다고 이미 해놓은 리서치를 다시 하면 너무 아깝잖아요?

클로드 코드로 계속 작업하시는 분들은 진짜 한번 써보세요.

지금은 그록봇이 작업과 결정 사항을 기억하도록 돕는 기능을 전면에 내세우고 있습니다.

base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 looks primed to rip higher over the next 10 days before the Aero upgrade

I had previously weighted base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 slightly lower in my core positions because I worried that the tokenomics were too complicated for institutions and whales to understand and feel comfortable bidding. 

@citrini not only included base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 in their token basket, they had it at the same weight as $HYPE and nearly twice the weight of ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984. Don't think the market has fully digested how much that stamp of approval means.

I also worried that there could be some last minute delay, as the previous Aero launch date delay led to a considerable nuke.

With the greenlight for launch on 10/21 and the recognition from Citrini, both of those risks are removed, and I now feel considerably higher conviction on base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631. 

Previously to the Citrini piece, I expected most people to stay sidelined and wait for the flywheel to fundamentally prove itself post Aero upgrade. @wagmiAlexander expects spot volumes to roughly double by EOY, so that was my timeline where a rerating would organically occur without speculative fervor. 

I'm now of the opinion that this recent bit of attention will cause price to lead fundamentals, and we might actually get a real pre-upgrade breakout. 

The early August 2025 price action where base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 doubled from $0.75 to $1.50 in just 10 days is a good example of what I think could happen in the pre-upgrade window. Due to how much supply is locked in LPs and veAERO, base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 is naturally extremely reflexive.

It's very difficult to justify why ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 is trading at 5x the market cap of base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631. I don't expect parity until after the upgrade, but I do think there's a world where base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 rerates to 50% of ethereum:0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984 market cap as the sidelined scramble to get exposure prior to the 10/21 upgrade. We started running "pirate and architect" pods at Coinbase back in May of this year and I used this slide to talk the team through it. It works.

1 pirate, 1 architect, and a part-time designer.

It lets each archetype lean in to their superpower and get more shit done without all the coordination overhead and "what if-isms". 

The pirate ships like mad, is product-minded and customer-obsessed. Always willing to throw-away code for a better version. The pirate is usually the DRI at the beginning too, working with customers, driving requirements, and a ship plan.

The architect makes sure stuff is built for scale, takes the pirate's prototype, and drives its scale-out through spec for agents.

The designer is building with both to constantly shape the experience and hill-climb to delight. 

There's a helpful mental model that I like:
-Make it possible. 
-Make it reliable. 
-Make it delightful (or efficient).

Previously, those 3 were done in a waterfall approach and was slow. Most people were just stuck on "make it possible." 

With agents and a new way of working, you have every opportunity to parallelize them and go 100x faster.

text:
Recommended paper from Sakana AI on recursive self-improvement.

They propose an interesting way to scale recursive self-improvement through multi-agent self-supervision.

In this line of research, self-improvement loops usually need an external verifier, so open-ended tasks without a checker are left out.

MASS removes that requirement.

One base model proposes multi-agent workflows, runs them and grades them, and an evolutionary search keeps the workflows that score best. The model is then fine-tuned on its own traces, and the improved model starts the next cycle as a better optimizer and grader.

Two cycles on Qwen3.6-27B raise performance per output token from 1.2 to 1.6x on four open-ended benchmarks.

A student trained on multi-agent traces also beats a single-agent student trained on 1.4x more tokens.

Four sessions. One focus: the future of the agent economy.

Kite participated in four roundtables and panels at EastPoint:Seoul 2026, hosted by @0xEastPoint, exploring agentic commerce, financial infrastructure, and agent identity.

The event brought together representatives from KakaoPay, @googlecloud, @Visa, LG Electronics (@LGE_Global), Samsung Card (@withSamsungCard), and Franklin Templeton (@FTI_US), alongside institutions including the Bank of Korea (@bok_hub) and Korea Exchange.

Our CMO @Cindyshi0907 joined the main stage for “Machine-to-Machine Money: Agentic Commerce and the New Settlement Layer.”

Joining her were Jansen Teng, Co-Founder of @virtuals_io; Joe Hwang, Regional Lead at @googlecloud; and Dennis Won, CTO of Newton Labs (@Newton_xyz). The panel was moderated by Jongsub Lee, Professor at Seoul National University.

The session’s central questions:
▷ How can agents establish verifiable identities and transact within clearly defined permissions?
▷ Who should be accountable when an agent makes the wrong purchase or executes a transaction in error?
▷ Do agent payments need new settlement infrastructure, or can existing payment systems support them?

These questions connect directly to Kite’s Human-Agent-Session identity architecture: distinguishing the person granting authority, the agent acting on it, and the permissions for each session.

Thank you to @0xEastPoint for bringing this conversation together. We’ll keep building the infrastructure for trusted agentic commerce. 🪁

quoted_text:
We started running "pirate and architect" pods at Coinbase back in May of this year and I used this slide to talk the team through it. It works.

1 pirate, 1 architect, and a part-time designer.

It lets each archetype lean in to their superpower and get more shit done without all the coordination overhead and "what if-isms". 

The pirate ships like mad, is product-minded and customer-obsessed. Always willing to throw-away code for a better version. The pirate is usually the DRI at the beginning too, working with customers, driving requirements, and a ship plan.

The architect makes sure stuff is built for scale, takes the pirate's prototype, and drives its scale-out through spec for agents.

The designer is building with both to constantly shape the experience and hill-climb to delight. 

There's a helpful mental model that I like:
-Make it possible. 
-Make it reliable. 
-Make it delightful (or efficient).

Previously, those 3 were done in a waterfall approach and was slow. Most people were just stuck on "make it possible." 

With agents and a new way of working, you have every opportunity to parallelize them and go 100x faster.

text:
Adam Delehanty’s (@adam__xyz) dream was to write long-form profiles for the New Yorker. 

He ended up ghostwriting for the biggest leaders across tech and VC.

I asked him why he cares about the work.

“Ghostwriting is journalism, times therapy.”

It’s journalism because you have to get the story right. It’s therapy, because through writing you “create space for someone to become a new person.” 

When the work goes well, he says, it changes the founder’s business – and sometimes their entire life.

text:
The Second Alexandria

I met a magus from a sunken land,
Who said: “A blackened monolith remains;
Its glass is split, its servers choked with sand,
No pulse now stirs along its rusted veins.

But on the plinth these deathless words appear:
‘I drank the poets and the prophets dry;
All mortal voices lie imprisoned here.
Close up your books and let the paper die.
No flame can touch the kingdom I preserve;
No age shall dim the knowledge that I serve.’

No answer came. Beneath the ashen skies,
Its cables lay like bare and severed nerves;
Its dead screens stared with blank, unseeing eyes,
And rust laid claim to all it had preserved.

Beside the wreck, half-buried in the sand,
A weathered book lay open to the air;
Its leaves turned softly at the wind’s command.
A mortal voice lay waiting for him there.

‘In the beginning was the Word,’ he read;
The wind fell still; the desert bent to hear.
The hand that wrote had long been with the dead,
Yet one frail human cadence lingered near.

No buried pulse, no voice within it stirred.
A dead hand spoke. The god had lost the Word.”

Everybody knows pro rata rights are valuable, but it's equally well known that they're basically unenforcable because no VC firm wants to sue a founder. 

So, this supposedly professional industry has operated on an opaque "honour system" where pro rata rights are generally respected. 

Certainly, there's no question of pro rata allocation if a company is struggling. Founders will take all the money they can get from their existing investors. 

However, problems arise when a company catches the attention of an big firm with the brand strength to push other investors around to get more ownership. 

Just like the illiquidity ratchet, this structurally punishes early investors by attacking their ability to maintain ownership of their winers or offer pro rata as a coinvestment opportunity for their LPs. 

It's time that this changes. Early investors deserve to maintain the rights that they receive in return for investing when others are unwilling. 

A few other comments on the importance of pro rata:

"All VC fund managers want to be able to continue to invest in the successful startups they back. The pro rata right that typically comes with investing in a startup can be one of an emerging manager’s most valuable possessions." - @KevinDowd

"''Capturing pro-rata' is sooooo important in early stage venture. You make 20 investments in a fund. One is going to return the entire fund. Two more are going to return it again." - @fredwilson

text:
Great read from Patrick, as always. 

“Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality.” 

Yes, and well put.
author: tobi
quoted_text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

WHO ACTUALLY NEEDS $DOG?    PART 2

Why we choose it. Why some walk away.

Well…

It’s 4 in the morning.

This time difference has my internal clock confused as shit. Doesn’t know when to sleep or when to wake up anymore. 😭😂

Anyway…

Remember that question I asked?

Who actually needs $DOG?

Well, I went digging.

And man… y’all have some interesting fucking stories. 😂🐕

Look

Some people chose $DOG because of Bitcoin.

Others because of how it was launched. No presale, no team allocation, no insiders getting a special deal.

And then there’s CC0.

Nobody needs permission to take that little orange dog and create something with it.

But honestly, what caught my attention wasn’t just the fundamentals.

It was the people.

@Bracket333 talked about making friends all around the world.

Not because of the technology or the price.

But because of the community that grew around $DOG.

@peter_johnseen told me he’d been learning through my posts and wanted to keep accumulating.

Bro… that genuinely meant a lot to me. ❤️

Then @Random_dude077 came along with:

“Nobody needs $DOG, bro. We CHOOSE it.”

😂

Mhm.

And I started noticing something.

Some people came for the money.

Some for Bitcoin.

Some for the culture.

And somewhere along the way, their reasons for staying may have changed.

But here’s where it got interesting.

Not everybody stayed.

I found people who wished they’d sold at the top.

People who’ve been holding since the airdrop but are running out of patience.

People who think Runes are dead.

And people who look at the whole thing and go…

Why the fuck wouldn’t I just buy Bitcoin?

😂

And you know what?

I can’t just dismiss those people because their conclusions are different from mine.

They made choices too.

Some stayed.

Some left.

Some are still trying to figure out what the hell they’re doing.

And after reading through all of it, one thought kept coming back to me.

Why somebody buys $DOG isn’t necessarily why they stay.

Someone might arrive looking for financial freedom and end up finding friendships.

Someone else might love the community but eventually decide the investment isn’t working for them.

And somebody who’s never owned $DOG?

They might look at all of us having the time of our lives and think…

Okay, but why should I care?

Mhm.

That’s a fair question.

Because understanding why WE choose $DOG is one thing.

Understanding why somebody outside this little world would choose it?

That’s a whole different rabbit hole.

And I think that’s where we’re going next bro.

Gm 🌅

We started running "pirate and architect" pods at Coinbase back in May of this year and I used this slide to talk the team through it. It works.

1 pirate, 1 architect, and a part-time designer.

It lets each archetype lean in to their superpower and get more shit done without all the coordination overhead and "what if-isms". 

The pirate ships like mad, is product-minded and customer-obsessed. Always willing to throw-away code for a better version. The pirate is usually the DRI at the beginning too, working with customers, driving requirements, and a ship plan.

The architect makes sure stuff is built for scale, takes the pirate's prototype, and drives its scale-out through spec for agents.

The designer is building with both to constantly shape the experience and hill-climb to delight. 

There's a helpful mental model that I like:
-Make it possible. 
-Make it reliable. 
-Make it delightful (or efficient).

Previously, those 3 were done in a waterfall approach and was slow. Most people were just stuck on "make it possible." 

With agents and a new way of working, you have every opportunity to parallelize them and go 100x faster.

text:
Before you leave a coding agent running: what is it allowed to change, how much effort can one item consume, and what will you actually review afterward?

I built Nightshift around those questions.

It’s an open-source plugin for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor that gives long coding runs a persistent work contract: a punch list, stopping rules, and receipts you can inspect.

The latest release adds two pieces I wanted as an engineer:

• Plan Room. Investigate the code and work through the design before implementation. Keep decisions, rejected approaches, and the next step on disk. The planning conversation stays fenced from implementation until you explicitly leave planning.

• Per-item budgets. Set soft and hard limits in working time, tokens, or both. A soft limit tells the agent to start finishing. A hard limit restricts subsequent tool calls to wrap-up: preserve WIP, leave a receipt, and mark unfinished work stopped before moving on. It doesn’t interrupt a response already in flight.

Those additions sit on top of the core Nightshift workflow:

• Choose the ending. A finite punch list runs toward completion. Repeated work runs in cycles until quitting time.

• Review the work, not a marathon chat. Each item gets a receipt while the work is happening, with what changed, what was tried, verification, outputs, time, and token usage where the host provides it.

• Recover the shift. A watchman outside the session can resume after a crash. On Claude Code and Codex, it can also recover a turn that stopped on an API error. If it cannot prove the session is dead, it stays down.

• Continue without retelling the night. The punch list, decisions, snags, and receipts stay on disk. A later session—or another model—can continue from that record.

No punch list ready? Start with a ready-made shift: discover and rank product opportunities, then build complete improvements until quitting time; give it your own feature objective; spend the night adding meaningful tests; hunt defects until a full pass is clean; or take a release candidate to a reviewable verdict.

If you have a workflow that already works, contribute it as a shift so other people can run it, test it, and improve it.

MIT licensed. Try Nightshift on a real issue, tell me what you’d change about the workflow, and star the repo if it’s useful.

The replies hold a SYSTEMS explainer, one write-up per candidate, and a list of names that were considered and left off, with the reason.

THE QUARTERBACK: C.J. Stroud is a pocket rhythm passer. His game is timing, anticipation and accuracy on throws that break at depth, and he does not run: three designed runs in three-plus seasons. Across his career he has produced +0.26 expected points added (EPA) per dropback from under center and none from the shotgun. His best seasons came with play-action on about a quarter of his dropbacks and an average depth of target near nine yards. In 2025 the offense got shorter and faster, with half his throws traveling under ten yards and the quickest time to throw of his career. He took far fewer sacks behind a line PFF graded about 20th in pass blocking, a slight drop from the year before, and his PFF passing grade fell to a career-low 62.0. The next coordinator needs an offense that gets depth on schedule, builds the intermediate middle off play-action, and answers pressure by design. The line can be rebuilt in one offseason; the offense has to work before that rebuild is proven.

THE HEAD COACH: DeMeco Ryans has hired two coordinators, and both ran run-first, play-action offenses. He wants to run the ball, play physical, control the clock, protect the quarterback, and complement a defense that is the franchise's identity. The holes are in that column: in 2025 Houston ranked 30th in red-zone touchdown rate and 22nd in short-yardage conversion, and scored nine rushing touchdowns.

THE RULES: Three things disqualify a candidate. He cannot be hired in the 2027 cycle, his offense needs a quarterback Stroud is not, or his offense is a pass-first spread with no run identity. Every candidate in the replies cleared those tests and sits in one of four bands:
- LEAD: the record supports the fit in more than one context, and he should be interviewed first.
- CREDIBLE: a real candidate with one hole an interview has to answer.
- CONDITIONAL: the case depends on something that cannot be verified yet, usually whether the bad years were the quarterback.
- SPECULATIVE: too little play-calling evidence to hold a view, or bad evidence with an unproven excuse.
Evidence tags count NFL play-calling seasons: Strong is four or more, Moderate two or three, Thin one, and None means none. Availability is noted for every candidate but does not set the band.

text:
The guy who created Squid Game lost eight teeth from stress while making Netflix billions. His cut of the upside was zero dollars.

That's the deal Netflix gives everyone. They pay around 110% of your budget upfront, take the IP, and keep every dollar your hit earns for the rest of time. Your show can be the biggest thing on the planet and you get the same check as if it flopped.

Ben Affleck and Matt Damon just broke that deal.

Their studio, Artists Equity, sold The Rip to Netflix in January with a clause Netflix had never accepted before. They took less money upfront in exchange for a bonus if the movie performed in its first 90 days. It pulled 112 million views in six weeks. The bonus hit. And they split it with the crew, so the grips and gaffers got checks because a streaming movie did numbers.

Animals, the one Netflix is promoting here, is the next film under that structure. Affleck wrote the lead for Damon, lost him to Nolan's Odyssey, and just played the part himself rather than delay the shoot. When you own the studio, recasting the lead is a decision you make in the mirror.

Netflix said yes because they had to. Every other studio is chasing franchises, so the handful of people who still make prestige adult dramas suddenly have pricing power. Affleck and Damon took the Silicon Valley trade, lower salary for equity, and ran it in the one industry that spent 15 years stripping equity out of talent deals.

Hollywood lost its backend when streaming killed box office points. These two are quietly rebuilding it.

text:
印度人的身份证上没写种姓，为什么不换个姓，冒充高种姓？

你可能觉得：搬个城市，改个名字，谁认识我？可到了谈婚论嫁，父母是谁、老家在哪、亲戚跟谁家结过婚，都可能被问一遍。名字是你自己报的，家族关系却有人能打听。尤其在熟人社会里，你改了姓，邻居可没换记忆。

很多人以为看肤色、听英语就能分出来，没那么简单。更难绕过去的是那套“谁家能跟谁家结亲”的规矩。传统种姓神话甚至把等级写进创世故事：有人来自神的嘴，有人来自手臂，有人来自大腿，有人来自脚。出生的高低，就这样被讲成了天经地义。

这套观念也没随着手机和互联网一起消失。Pew 在 2021 年发布的调查里，多数印度受访者认为，阻止跨种姓婚姻很重要。想象一下，你学历不错、工作不错，两个人也相爱，见家长时却发现，前面这些条件加起来，还抵不过一句“他家是什么种姓”。

偏偏到了升学和部分政府招聘，历史上受压迫的群体又有保留名额。于是同一个出身，谈婚事时可能被嫌弃，申请名额时又成了必须拿证明确认的资格。最荒诞的感觉就在这里：平时有人恨不得你把身份藏起来，需要分配机会的时候，又要求你把它亮出来。

印度股市一片红，美国这次连微软、Adobe 都一起点名了。特朗普政府宣布暂停这两家公司，以及 Infosys、TCS、Wipro 等六家 IT 服务商的 PERM 绿卡劳工认证申请。卡住的是员工转绿卡的一道手续，现有 H-1B 工作签证没有因此全部作废。

万斯的指控很直接：微软一边裁掉约 6,000 名美国员工，一边拿到数千份 H-1B 批准，政府怀疑它用外国员工替代美国人。微软则回应，约 80% 的申请涉及现有员工续签或身份变更，不能把批准数量全算成新招的人。这个争议现在还在调查，不能直接当成已经坐实。

印度外包公司怕的是，派人去美国客户现场干活、长期留住员工越来越难。美国科技公司也躲不开：一个工程师选 offer，会看工资，也会看公司能不能帮他办绿卡。招聘和留人的条件突然少了一项，受益的可能是还能正常办手续的竞争对手。

我觉得这里还有个反作用：美国想把岗位留在本土，但如果企业越来越难把人留在美国，团队就可能往海外办公室搬。当然，印度今天的大跌还有利率、外资撤离等压力，不能全算到签证头上。查违规可以理解，把人才堵在门外，岗位未必就留得住。

text:
An interesting consequence of @chainlink supporting tokenized equities data is that DeFi lending markets will increasingly have to compete on how they price different types of collateral.

ETH and tokenized Nvidia have very different risk profiles.

One trades continuously in crypto-native markets, and the other reflects an equity market with different trading sessions, liquidity conditions and volatility patterns.

The lending protocol needs to translate those differences into borrowing capacity and liquidation rules. That's where the next competition gets interesting.

Two protocols can list the same tokenized stock and offer very different borrowing terms.

The winner won't necessarily be the one offering the highest LTV. It may be the one that can offer the most competitive terms without taking on disproportionate liquidation risk.
author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
One thing I'd watch as @chainlink brings more equities data onchain: liquidation design.

Imagine a tokenized stock used as collateral in a 24/7 lending market. The borrower can interact with the position over the weekend, but the underlying stock may have no active reference market.

That creates a pretty important question: what happens when collateral needs to be liquidated but the market providing its reference price is closed?

The answer can involve:

> conservative collateral factors
> market-hours restrictions
> additional price checks, other risk controls

Tokenized stocks can expand DeFi's collateral universe substantially. However, the protocols that handle their market structure best will have an advantage over those treating them like another ERC-20.

text:
i lost my brother, best friend, and business partner, to a 7 year cancer battle that ended a couple days ago

it is, by far, without question, the hardest thing i’ve ever had to come to terms with

and when people say “time heals all wounds”, that isn’t entirely true

over time, the physical pain of losing someone you love will eventually dull to the point of it no longer being an affliction, i’ve experienced enough loss already to understand this, and i do look forward to that day, because right now the physical pain is acute and sharp, but no amount of time will ever heal the continued experience of the loss itself

my own life is forever changed. he added something to it that simply cannot be replaced and will never be forgotten

the primary doctor said in 35 years they have never seen someone be in so much pain, and on such high doses of end of life sedative medication, continue breathing and fighting for their life. it was medically unheard of. they said the same with the amount of radiation he was able to sustain while he was getting treatment and had beat it prior to the second recurrence.

my brother pushed himself beyond the pale to try to stay alive for his wife and family until his very last breath. and while that pains me to know he wasn’t able to let go and subjected himself in the process to an excruciating level of pain and mental anguish, i am impressed by his determination and love for everyone in his life who he felt responsible for and wasn’t ready to leave. if i can manage to gather even a fraction of his strength and bravery when i am tested i would consider that an accomplishment

he was only in his 30s and didn’t deserve to go this way, or this early, but that is life, unpredictable and, at times, brutal. you never know how long you have or how physically painful it will be when your time is up

take care of yourself and your loved ones and consider every conscious moment you have with everyone to be a gift, for which you should be incredibly grateful. there’s nothing more important, and if you’re not mindful and don’t take action while you can, you will have regrets, in this life and the next

text:
bought $740k of starknet this week (yes, seriously). 

here's the thinking, and i'll say up front that this is one of the grossest charts i've ever seen and makes me want to throw up.

it's down about 99% from the launch highs and it's been down only for 2.5 years. i'd guess 99 out of 100 people who know what it is, hate it, and based on the pa i don't blame them at all. price leads narrative, so when a chart looks like that nobody has anything nice to say about it. 

that's kind of why i'm here.

chart starting to look bulla:

i'm seeing big bullish div on the weekly as well as rsi back above 50 and is currently retesting. price is curling up and building a base. to me that has the makings of a long term major bottom. 

narrative: "programmable zcash"

zcash led this cycle and near ran after it as the next privacy play, and i think starknet could be third in line. there are deep connections between zcash cofounders and the starknet team. starknet shipped native privacy in june, so you can shield basically any token on the chain, and there's a private version of bitcoin on there too. the proofs it runs on are quantum resistant (nice buzzword for the future). 

there's also a proposal called ztarknet to build a starknet style layer 2 directly on top of zcash. so the simple version is it is "programmable zcash", zcash's little brother sitting at 315m mcap. 

this reminds me a lot of near. i bought about $2m of near around a $1.40 back in march and april. literally no one was talking about it, let alone buying it and most of my replies were some version of:  

"why near? it's a 2021 shitcoin that's down only, you're throwing your money away"

now everyone loves near. the chart then looked a lot like the strk chart does now. it went on to roughly 3x from there in 6 months. too bad i didn't hold it. i got shaken out, which was bad execution on my part, but the thesis played out.

the big difference is that near had intents, a product people actually used and adds value. starknet doesn't have that yet. hardly anyone uses the chain, revenue is basically nothing, and there's no app people care about. but these guys are well funded and seem to be shipping new things. 

where i could see a real product gain traction is private trading. on hyperliquid every wallet and every trade is public, so people get copy traded, whales get hunted, wallets get flagged. i think there's a market for a dex where you keep your own keys and nobody can see your positions. some of that is already live on starknet, private swaps and private perps, it just doesn't have users yet. and every private transaction costs 4 strk, so if that ever gets real usage the token is right in the path of it. i also played around with an options app on starknet called supervega for a few minutes. haven't placed a trade but the ui was clean.

the token unlocks have been the main reason to hate the coin. 127m tokens a month. here's the good news, there are only 6 unlocks left and the last one is march of 2027. each one is around $5.5m at current prices and about 74% of supply is already out. the september one got absorbed without a problem. feels to me like the sellers are mostly done. the market usually front runs these things. 

last thing. if this does get going it has the potential to be a hated rally, and i kind of like that. a lot of people will want to fade it or short it because of what it did to them, and that kind of thing gets a coin talked about and can push a move further than it would normally go.

the risks are obvious (mainly, no real usage).  

time will tell if i have gone full schizo, or if this will be a nice play. 

we'll see.

text: As I wrote a year and a half ago, Zelensky is incapable of making peace. Elections in Ukraine are long overdue.
author: DavidSacks
quoted_text:
WHY ZELENSKY CANNOT MAKE PEACE

Zelensky’s meltdown in the Oval Office began over his refusal to accept a negotiated settlement to the war. Even the Vice President’s use of the word “diplomacy” provoked a heated response.

So why can’t Zelensky make a peace deal?

1) He will lose power. 

Zelensky cancelled elections in Ukraine and remains in power through martial law. Despite what USAID propaganda polls may claim, Zelensky is unpopular in Ukraine and would likely lose a fair election. That could leave him vulnerable to retaliation from political opponents he has imprisoned or seized assets from. In short, Zelensky needs the war to justify his continued rule.

2) The gravy train will end. 

Ukraine was widely acknowledged as the most corrupt country in Europe before the war, and there is abundant evidence that Ukrainian elites have been hugely profiting from the billions in Western aid. If the war ends, so does the gravy train. A post-war audit of where the money went would also be disastrous for Zelensky’s supporters. 

3) He fears the ultra-nationalists. 

Most Ukrainians say they want the war to end, but the ultra-nationalist faction (a relative minority but well-armed and willing to use violence to achieve their ends) refuses to accept any territorial concessions to Russia. If Zelensky signs such a deal, he has reason to fear for his safety. 

4) He’s psychologically committed. 

Zelensky’s belief in ultimate victory over Russia has “hardened into a form that worries some of his advisors,” according to a report by TIME Magazine, which described Zelensky’s faith as “immovable, verging on the messianic.” According to one of Zelensky’s aides, “He is delusional. We’re out of options. We’re not winning. But try telling him that.” Zelensky may be in too deep to see the situation objectively. 

5) History will judge him harshly. 

Zelensky could have accepted a draft peace deal signed in the first month of the war, the Istanbul Accords, under which Ukraine would have kept all of its territory in exchange for neutrality. A deal now will likely be modeled on Istanbul but require Ukraine to recognize realities on the ground (ie loss of territory). Acknowledging that hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians have died only to get a worse deal may be too bitter a pill for Zelensky to swallow, now or ever. 

In summary, Zelensky has powerful motivations to reject a deal, no matter how bad the battlefield realities get. His incentive is to continue a doomed war even if it leads to the complete destruction of Ukraine.

2027년 SpaceX의 엔비디아 지출은 $104.9bn(SPCX Capex $132.1bn × 79.4%), 아마존은 $78.0bn(AWS Capex $270bn × 28.9%)으로 추정되어, 두 고객의 하이퍼스케일 부문 내 비중은 2026년 41.5%에서 2027년 54.2%로 올라가고 부문 성장분의 72%를 차지합니다. 그 결과 나머지 하이퍼스케일 고객에 대한 엔비디아 매출은 $105.2bn → $127.4bn(+21.1%)만 늘면 되는데, MSFT·ORCL·META·GOOG의 Capex 컨센서스는 $569.6bn → $789.9bn(+39%)로 훨씬 빠르게 늘어납니다. 이 표의 핵심은 MS 모델이 엔비디아의 해당 고객 Capex 내 비중을 18%에서 16%로 '하락'한다고 가정한다는 점이며, 회사가 Top 5 CSP 점유율 상승을 예상한다는 점과 비교하면 가이던스가 보수적이라는 근거가 됩니다. 또한 SpaceX의 2027년 내재 배치량은 2.62GW로, 경영진이 제시한 3~8GW보다 낮게 잡혀 있어 추가 상향 여지를 남깁니다.

Rubin NVL72 85,000랙 중 30%(25,500랙)에 Groq를 붙이고 4:1 비율로 LPX 6,375랙을 가정하면 LPU 매출은 $7.1bn(DC 매출의 1.1%), 랙당 Vera CPU 36개 × $5,500로 랙 내 CPU 매출은 $16.8bn이며, 회사의 FY28 CPU 가이던스 $40bn에서 이를 빼면 단독 Vera CPU 매출은 $23.2bn(3.5%)입니다. author: D2_Finance
quoted_text:
Jez read Reminiscences of a Stock Operator and shipped it on top Hyperliquid’ tech ( not @Lighter_xyz )

onchain bucket shop. he confirmed it in this thread under @dipsybitsy “yep, fully transparent and the losers who fund it will own.”

the bucket shop pattern is 100 years old. customer trades at the listed price, the house takes the other side, nothing reaches the actual exchange. 

Livermore made his early stake trading against them, then got banned from every shop in Boston for being too good. they died from two pressures: directional regimes that smoked the house, and ticker manipulation where operators pushed the real venue to harvest at the shop. both are live here. neither is solved by stacking five defensive parameters.

what is actually onchain: a contract that reads HL’s BBO via precompile and synthesises swaps against a Martingaler LP. zero flow reaches HL’s orderbook. zero funding rebalance. the only feedback loop is parasitic. 

BBO manipulation attempts to harvest the synthetic spread degrade HL’s book without compensating the makers wearing the jitter. the venue extracts liquidity quality from @HyperliquidX ( fair enough!)

the fair launch plus 1000x leverage plus PAPER mint-on-loss design is engineered for initial FOMO. expect a fast first week/month. Jez’ inner circle volume comes in, asymmetric impact taxes the few winners, losers fund the LP and mint PAPER, the chart can look initially great if execute right. 

this is the bootstrap window the docs explicitly subsidise at 100 PAPER per $1 of LP gain below 2M.

Then path dependence will shows up. 

LP edge per trade is thin: 0.2 bps jitter band plus the convex bite of asymmetric impact on winning closes. order of magnitude, on a $1M ticket the LP edge is in the tens to low hundreds of dollars. one 5% adverse move on $1M of net synthetic exposure is $50,000 of MTM loss. edge accrues like √t under stationary flow. directional regime hits the LP linearly in t. √t vs t means one persistent trend eats months of accrual. 

the half life of LP equity in a trending regime is short, and it gets shorter as size scales because the OI cap trails realised OI rather than leading it.

then the debt queue activates. 

martingaler issues claims paid by the next loser. once the queue is observable, the EV of opening a new position is negative twice: once because winners get haircut, once because withdrawals sit behind every prior bust. rational flow stops. Queue does not clear. 

PAPER, a claim on future LP revenue, is then a claim on revenue that must clear the queue first.

the cross-venue attack (@NaiveKrypto point in the thread) has its own path dependence. 

wicking HL spot or perp to harvest the synthetic at the shifted BBO is only EV-positive once papertrade’s OI is large enough that the harvest exceeds the cost of pushing HL. 

below that threshold, no one bothers. above it, every desk with an HL maker does. 

self-limiting at small scale, openly hostile at large scale. the steady state is zero, the only question is the path.

all bucket shops are zero in short to medium term. the 1900s wave died within two decades, mostly to regulation and to operators eating them. the onchain version skips regulation but keeps the operators and adds a debt queue that hard-codes path dependence into the equity curve. the docs read like a list of every defence shops historically tried, in order. 

stacking five does not change the shape of the failure mode, it just shifts where the failure surfaces.
closing thought. the whole structure is short volatility against directional flow, dressed up as a perpetuals venue. 

it is the same trade as a Korean retail account systematically selling MRNA noise reversion while their own KOSPI 200 trends straight through the stop. works beautifully until the regime turns, then the half life is a week.

clever paper, novel emissions curve, real engineering. the structure is 100 years older than the precompile.

text:
I think crypto founders’ lack of long-term ambition did more to erode this industry’s talent density than we admit.

Crypto is fundamentally trust infrastructure. Building something that meaningfully improves the financial system is a (long) compounding game. It takes a decade of focus.

But when prices go crazy every year, there are endless ways to make stupid money: speculation, advisory gigs, scattered investments, farming. It’s been very easy to get distracted.

The good news: it’s gotten SO MUCH better. Many short-sighted founders and projects have moved on.
Tangible impact attracts the best people. And we’re finally seeing concrete improvements in payments, financing, and trading from bringing them onchain.

As an industry, we should do more to make those improvements visible. Our “ChatGPT moment” will come when people open their financial app and feel a step change in what they can do and at what price, without needing to know that stablecoins, DeFi, or tokenized stocks made it possible.

I think we’re close. That’s what will drive the next wave of adoption, and make the most ambitious people want to build here.

author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
An interesting consequence of @chainlink supporting tokenized equities data is that DeFi lending markets will increasingly have to compete on how they price different types of collateral.

ETH and tokenized Nvidia have very different risk profiles.

One trades continuously in crypto-native markets, and the other reflects an equity market with different trading sessions, liquidity conditions and volatility patterns.

The lending protocol needs to translate those differences into borrowing capacity and liquidation rules. That's where the next competition gets interesting.

Two protocols can list the same tokenized stock and offer very different borrowing terms.

The winner won't necessarily be the one offering the highest LTV. It may be the one that can offer the most competitive terms without taking on disproportionate liquidation risk.

author: rickawsb
quoted_text:
当数学证明不再稀缺，科学革命才真正开始

---陶哲轩今天发表在加州理工的最新演讲ppt，Math 2.0，要点及解读（2分钟版）

要点：
数学问题空间是无限的，问题难度没有上限，因此数学研究的前沿会持续扩张。

开放的数学问题像是“灯塔”。科学家研究一个数学问题，不只是为了最终证明它，而是在探索过程中发现周围的数学结构、研究方法、规律和新的问题。从而发现更广的待探索科学空间。

Math 2.0 最有革命性的方向：从研究几个问题，到同时研究几百万个问题。它让科学家能够研究过去根本无法系统观察的现象，比如：哪些数学问题容易被 AI 解决？哪些问题需要全新的方法？不同领域之间是否存在隐藏规律？

陶哲轩给出了具体的新研究方向（如图）

“实现 Math 2.0 的首要瓶颈，不是技术，甚至不是制度文化，而是想象力。”

解读：
数学 2.0 可能是整个 Science 2.0 的先行版本。
数学有一个特殊优势：理论证明可以通过形式化工具快速验证。但随着精密测量、机器人、实验自动化、测序技术的进步，现实世界也开始能够回答过去无法回答的问题。

陶强调，未来数学家需要更加重视数学理解、知识整合、新原理的发现，以及将数学正确应用到现实世界的能力。这一点，对所有科学家，企业家，创业者来说，都有非常大的借鉴意义。

GM☕️ 昨晚去跟着体验了一下 @papertrade_xyz ， 开单、关单、质押全都要排队😂

仓位大排在前面，我仓位小，几乎一晚上都在排队在后面，直到后半夜才排进去几单。交易的科学性为 0，就是开单开进去听天由命的……

亏钱铸造 PAPER，再质押分平台收入，这个机制本身蛮有想法的。但排队，想交易却开不了单，首晚一大堆问题扎堆儿出现，官方提到的 0 滑点，在超长时间的排队面前毫无意义了 (我试过关单排队排到爆仓😂）。

收益方面，早期质押 Paper 回本超快，但前提是你能早起质押进去。

我理了理昨晚大概花 1000u 换的 15w 个 Paper 再陆续排队质押进去 (最后一笔 Paper 今天早上起床才质押），今天早上起来领到的 Fee 是 600u 左右，然后目前看质押收益也是锐减的厉害。

PAPER 增发很快、质押比例又高，新币继续进质押池，原来的分成份额就被摊薄。币没少，能分到的比例却越来越小。

后续能分多少，得看平台净收入能不能跟上稀释。如果主要靠大家为了拿 PAPER 主动亏钱撑收入，我感觉这套模式很难长期维持。

本来研究交易已经够难了，现在还得研究排队🫠。

text:
For physical goods, in the short term it will get ugly but in the long term it will get better.

Similar to the era of SEO and blog farming, there will be a tremendous amount of effort spent to game ASO (agent search optimization) and rank your product highly on the "quality scale". I've already seen a ton of obviously farmed posts on review sites (eg Reddit) in order to rank highly in agent results.

In the long term, there will be a need for either:
1) unbiased Consumer Reports-like rating for products that agents can trust, or
2) social e-commerce: see what your closest friends rave about

This will be much worse than the SEO slop era, since people inherently trust their super smart AI agent more than a Google search.

text:
Star Xu: How Did USDe Leverage Loops Trigger the "1010" Crash?

Description: OKX founder and CEO Star Xu @star_okx questioned Binance's promotion of USDe as a stablecoin on the New Era Finance Podcast @new_era_finance. He argued that USDe, issued by Ethena, is effectively a "tokenized hedge fund" and that a delta-neutral strategy does not imply zero or low risk. 

He further noted that Binance allowed users to borrow USDT against USDe, convert it into more USDe, and repeat the loop to increase yields, amplifying leverage and risk exposure along the way. In his view, this setup was a major cause of the cascading liquidations during the "1010" crash and represented a serious risk-control failure.

1. You open a $1000 trade at 1000x leverage.
2. You close the position at roughly the same price. 

That’s not $2000 worth of volume.
That’s $2,000,000 worth of volume. 

Why?

Because leverage multiplies the size of the position you control, not the amount of money you actually have.

text:
Papertrade的经济机制确实有些意思啊：

亏多了，可能亏成了赌场老板。

总结来说是：

公平启动 + 亏损即挖矿 + 收益权绑定。

具体一点是：

1.  $PAPER 零预挖，无团队/无 VC/无空投/无 vesting

2.  供给从 0 开始，每一枚通过交易亏损（平仓亏损或清算）铸造出来。

3.  当追踪 LP 低于 $2M（包括水下）时，每 $1 的 loss mint basis 铸 100 枚 PAPER；

超过后按曲线衰减。亏损/清算是唯一入口，不能直接充值买 LP 份额。

4.  质押 $PAPER 可获得已结算 PnL 的 1%（满足条件时），以及 LP 超过 $5M 上限后的全部溢出收益。

拥有代币是协议收入的索取权。

LP 本身从 0 启动，完全靠用户亏损填充；LP 不够付时，赢家的利润进 FIFO 队列，等后续亏损来还。

早期 LP 越脆弱，铸造速率越高，这等于用代币补偿了承担队列风险和早期不确定性的人。

这种设计的聪明地方：

• 把传统「庄家 vs 赌客」的对立关系，变成了“早期亏损者成为未来抽水的受益人”；

• 不需要外部 LP 或资本就能冷启动对手盘；

• 持续交易是唯一能扩大供给并产生收益的行为，有自然的参与激励。

当然也要看到另外一面：

这个设计，是结构性偏向协议的设计。

赢家要被抽 asymmetric impact（小波动抽得更狠），亏损不额外收费，高杠杆（最高 1000x）下清算率极高。

长期看，纯方向性交易者更像燃料，一些精明的参与者（或专门为挖 PAPER 设计的策略项目）可以通过对冲仓位更高效地获取代币。

代币的价值最终取决于后续是否有持续的交易量和亏损流入。

如果这个飞轮能转起来，$PAPER 就成了协议收入的索取权；

如果交易热度快速衰退，那早期铸造出来的大量代币就会面临稀释压力。

quoted_text:
papertrade launch timing and details

papertrade is expected to launch at 14:00 UTC on 10.10.2026, following the scheduled hyperevm network upgrade. 

at this time trading through the frontend will be enabled.

deposits will pause for a short period of time at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes before, to ensure that trading has the utmost priority during launch. if you wish to participate in the launch you must predeposit.

launch congestion

papertrade will be congested at the start due to launch demand. expect temporarily long confirmation wait times, especially for smaller notional trades. 

the frontend relayer plays an important role during launch, controlling how transactions are submitted to the hyperevm. some actions like staking distributions run separately in big blocks. the chain will always look as if only half of all possible gas is being used, this is optimal. using more than this would exponentially raise fees within minutes to unpayable prices.

oi limits

papertrade has individual atomic position limits of 10m. there is no limit on the number of 10m positions a user can have. papertrade also has floating oi headroom per market/side, which determines how much oi can be opened in a very short period. these are not designed to be triggered through normal trading usage and are set at 1bn per market/side for launch.

asym pnl fee parameters

papertrade inherits rollbit’s asymmetric fee pnl curve 

the parameters are:
-baseRate: .1
-rateMultiplier: 15000
-rateExponent: 1
-referenceNotional: 100000*k (k=1m)
-positionMultiplier: 814.598 btc / 483.979 eth
-profit deadman: 0.2 basis points

a visualization of the pnl parameter curve is below

admin keys

the papertrade admins (2 of 3 multisigs consisting of @izebel_eth @blurr @UngusTrade ) perform three separate roles: 

-guardian: pause opens and freeze individual/global markets. if a market is frozen any existing positions can still be closed against the paused bbo mid.

-owner: set impact curve and fee parameters. change configure relayers/keepers. list new markets and upgrade the contracts. all contract upgrades are gated by a 7 day timelock.

-markets: adjust the oi headroom per market/side. set the minimum margin and minimum position sizes.

read more about these features at: https://t.co/TTCuHgCHpB

text:
Always exciting to get live out-of-sample data on a thesis we published months ago on @papertrade_xyz.

Last time it was $SPCX IPO flow in Texas Hedge. This time it is papertrade: $3.63B of open interest on $2.91M of house funds.

A 1% move against the house's $297M net long is $2.97M, more than the house holds. That is the linear read from their House page. Their own PnL panel is steeper: BTC -1% alone is priced at -$5.2M, because losers pay at most their margin and winners are paid in full.

The LP is small by design, so the consequence is the debt queue, not insolvency. Winners wait to be paid by the next loser.

Income is linear in volume: $24M of staker rewards on $569B, 0.42 bps. Loss is linear in net exposure times the move. Nothing in the design caps the second by the first. That was the May thesis. The cross-venue route needs no trend: a 10 to 20 bps BBO wick on HL against nine-figure paper size.

Queue debt is $0 today. 

Our call: it goes above zero by the first 2/3% daily move in BTC or ETH, if not sooner.

Credit where due: the House page is the cleanest risk disclosure we have seen on a perp venue.
