text:
Chamath says IP and software were "effectively rendered worthless" this week, after people decompiled Adobe's core products and published open-source versions, as every service goes headless

"The more important point I want to make though, is I sent this to Nick, there's been a couple things that happened in the last couple days, which I think are incredibly important."

"There have been people that decompiled the entire, the entire big five. What is the big five? Adobe has five very, very important products in their product suite. Freeberg may know them all, but I just know Photoshop. There's like a bunch of others. Okay."

"And these folks decompiled it, distilled it, and published open source versions of these things. And Rust, yeah. And I was so shocked, because I was like, hold on a second, these are like profound products that have existed and have had moats for years, and now they're just open source versions."

"And then Nikita was, I think, trolling, and he was building on that idea, and just talking about GTA, because it's about to get released. I think GTA 6 is about to come out, and we'll reconstruct this."

"Why is this important?"

"I think that IP and software was effectively rendered worthless two days ago."

"Because if you think about it, when everything is headless, so when Elon makes his services headless, Benioff made Salesforce headless a few months earlier, when all of these things are headless, and you can wrap them in agent tools, and you can connect them via MCP to other experiences, the value of IP does no longer exist in software. It doesn't exist."

"And I think that probably is the most profound implication."

"So, like, even in our business, we would argue with some of our customers all the time, because we'll say, oh, we'll build this for you, we'll own the IP. They'll say, no, we want the IP. We don't know how to negotiate it. And two days ago, I walked into the 8090 guys, I said, who cares? Who cares? But before, it was always a negotiation and a set of trade-offs. Now it's a who-cares thing, where, like, the IP is irrelevant."

"It still takes a while for the machinery of a business, and frankly the market, to understand. But that is the most important thing that happened this week in AI, in my opinion."

text:
If you want to make use of small pockets of time for development, I’ve found that the key isn’t:

“How much code can I write in 10 minutes?”

It’s:

“Can I get back into the work in under a minute?”

A surprising amount of short sessions gets wasted on questions like:

“What was I doing last time?”
“What did I ask this agent to do?”
“Which files are being changed?”

So I’ve been optimizing around three things:

1. Recover context in seconds
   → history, notes, progress

2. Make the next decision from your phone
   → launch agents, send follow-ups, orchestrate work

3. Inspect results without a laptop
   → browse files, code, Markdown, and HTML remotely

Once those are in place, the workflow changes:

10 minutes at lunch → dispatch the next issues
Back to the day job → agents keep working
Commute → check the results
Evening → resume by testing something that already moved forward

This is also how I’ve been shaping CommandMate.

The best way to use small pockets of time isn’t to code faster.
It’s to make sure even a few minutes are enough to move your AI team forward.

text:
昨天英文区都在刷屏讨论一个建立在 Hyperliquid 的 HyperEVM 上的新 Perp DEX 项目 @papertrade_xyz。

而之所以受关注，是因为项目启动时预存阶段吸引了 1.38 亿美元资金，开盘后几分钟内名义交易量就突破了百亿。

以及，一个带着浓厚资金盘设定的规则：亏钱即挖矿。

这个 DEX 开局自带1000倍杠杆，且0资金费率。
但开局时项目的 LP 是空的，也就是说你每一次开高杠杆爆仓亏掉的钱，会直接变成了庄家 LP 池的本金；

而作为补偿，协议会发给你代币$PAPER，让你变成它的“早期股东”，去分未来别人亏的钱。

在目前的极早期，每亏损 1 美元大约能换取 100 个 PAPER。质押这些 PAPER，就能分享协议对赢家抽成所产生的真实利润。

这就催生了一个荒诞的现象：

很多人故意开高杠杆去送钱爆仓，本质上是用确定的亏损，去“买”这个链上赌场的早期分红权。

这时你可能会问如果大家都赚钱，那 LP 池是空的，协议拿什么给大家钱呢？

根据其机制，赢家的本金可以直接退还，但利润需要进入一个排队系统（FIFO 队列）。

你赚了钱拿不走，必须等后面进场的新玩家爆仓亏钱了，资金池有了进账，才能按排队顺序把利润发给你。🤡

所以，目前冲进去“亏钱挖矿”的玩家，赌的是早期极高的代币红利，但项目飞轮很依赖后续源源不断的交易者进来亏钱输血。

那么你在这个 DEX 上亏多少钱就值得玩味了。亏少了，拿到的 PAPER 代币不够，质押分成可能也不多；

亏多了，考虑项目中长期风险，分给你的收入可能还抵不上你亏损的本金。

Papertrade 昨晚才正式上线，主打 1000 倍杠杆、零滑点、无资金费率，结果现在有交易员找到了专门收割LP 的漏洞。

先在 Papertrade 开巨额 ETH 空单。

再去 Hyperliquid 大量卖出 ETH，把订单簿中间价往下压约 0.1%。

quoted_text:
今晚币圈最疯狂的赌场开业了：MIT量化+链上巨鲸操刀，1000倍杠杆、亏钱挖矿，1小时交易量突破1000亿美元！

Papertrade上线约1小时，成交量突破1020亿美元，未平仓合约93.5亿美元，TVL约1.2亿美元。

平台根本就不需要任何初始做市资金，所有用户都跟协议对赌，用户亏得越多，协议的流动性池反而越大，亏损者还能拿到 PAPER，分享未来交易平台的收益。

创始人 Jez（@izebel_eth），2015年毕业于 MIT，学的是计算机与管理科学，后来在摩根士丹利工作了4年，还曾担任加密风投 Standard Crypto 的 Venture Partner，个人投资项目包括 FOMO、neutrl 等。

他还是一名扑克高手，2024年参加世界扑克巡回赛 WPT Prime Championship，最终拿到第7名，奖金18.6万美元。量化交易、VC投资、职业级扑克竞技经验，基本把金融市场、风险定价和博弈论凑齐了。

另一位创始人 Blurr（@blurr）更偏链上原生玩家，2017年前后进入 Crypto，经历过 CryptoKitties、Compound、Curve 等早期链上机会，还曾部署过 Refund（$RFD）。

Papertrade 的交易设计非常激进。它部署在 HyperEVM，利用预编译合约直接读取 Hyperliquid 订单簿买一卖一的中间价，以此合成 BTC、ETH 永续仓位，实际不会去 Hyperliquid 开对冲仓，所以没有传统资金费率、盘口滑点和点差。

听起来像免费交易，但盈利平仓会受到非对称收益折减，尤其针对极小价格波动的套利收益抽得更重。这套逻辑明显吸收了 Rollbit 的高杠杆赌场模型，只不过把定价、仓位和盈亏结算搬到了链上。

最有创造性的地方是 Martingaler 流动性自举机制。传统赌场必须先准备一大笔本金，才能赔付赢家。Papertrade 的 LP 从0美元启动，输家的亏损直接补充资金池。

如果庄家只有500万美元，而赢家需要领取600万美元盈利，协议可以先支付500万美元，剩余100万美元进入 FIFO 债务队列，等待未来交易者亏损后逐步偿还。

它用未来的亏损现金流解决初始资金不足的问题，但这笔债务不会凭空消失，极端情况下赢家可能长期拿不到全部利润。

再看 $PAPER，代币经济学才是这套设计的核心。没有预挖、没有团队和 VC 分配、没有空投，只有真实发生交易亏损或清算，才能铸造代币。

LP 追踪余额低于200万美元时，每亏损1美元最多按基础规则铸造100枚 PAPER，超过门槛后按照衰减曲线降低发行速度。

PAPER 质押者可以领取协议分配的 USDC 收益，当 LP 超过500万美元的目标余额后，超出部分的新增收益按机制分配给质押者。

PAPER 已发行约14.9亿枚，其中13.7亿枚被质押，累计质押奖励约24.8万美元。

Papertrade 可能是今年 Hyperliquid 生态最激进的一次交易所经济模型实验。它把做市商的收益、赌场的庄家优势和 DeFi 的代币激励揉进了同一个系统，甚至把普通交易者的亏损变成了协议融资手段。

Situation Update: Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger is reaching out to impacted users as part of the ongoing investigation. As a measure of precaution CryptoBilis confirmed it has ceased sales of all hardware wallet inventory until the investigation is concluded. text:
Cognition CEO Scott Wu predicts frontier AI models will handle only 2% of workloads but charge 98% gross margins as the other 98% becomes commoditized 

“The second thing I would say is doing a lot more model routing. Everyone is talking about model routing recently. It’s hot, obviously, but I would say it’s still very early.

“You don’t really need the Navier–Stokes guy to do everything. I think what we’re going to get to is a point where the absolute frontier models are running for about 2% of workloads. It could be 4% or 5%. The other 98% are running on models that are frankly much more commoditized, where there are many more options.

“Don’t worry, by the way. The frontier models themselves will probably be able to charge something like a 98% gross margin, so they’ll do just fine. But what that means is that doing really aggressive model routing and figuring out how to do that is really important.

“A year ago, even model routing was more of a meme than reality, if I’m being honest. If it wasn’t Sonnet 3.7 or Opus 4.1, or whatever was the best model at the time, you would feel that immediately as you started the session.

“At this point, you can see it really clearly in user behavior: you can swap out models and, most of the time, no one even notices. There are obviously specific tasks where you find and see the difference, but I think that’s increasingly going to be the case.”

针对 Veria AI 报告的支付引擎关键漏洞，RippleX 工程负责人 J. Ayo Akinyele 表示，XRP Ledger（XRPL）支付引擎存在超 10 年的严重漏洞，可导致 XRP 超出固定供应量被增发。该漏洞通过漏洞赏金计划发现，尚未被利用。开发团队已发布 xrpld 3.4.1 修复版本，并在公开披露前协调验证者完成网络升级。Akinyele 表示，AI 正加速漏洞发现速度，XRPL 将加大主动安全投入、清理技术债务、推进形式化验证，并系统性消除旧代码中的潜在风险。
author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
Security remains our top priority for preserving trust in the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Sharing a few thoughts following yesterday's disclosure of the critical payments engine vulnerability reported by Veria AI.

First, this was a serious vulnerability, and we don't take that lightly. The bug had existed in the codebase for over a decade and could have allowed XRP to be created beyond its fixed supply. Fortunately, it was discovered through our bug bounty program before it could ever be exploited.

Second, our response was fast and coordinated. The team developed and thoroughly tested a fix, worked closely with validators to rapidly upgrade the network, and secured the ledger before public disclosure. I'm proud of how everyone came together to address the vulnerability and protect the XRPL network.

But there's a much bigger lesson here.

AI is fundamentally changing how quickly vulnerabilities can be discovered. We have to move even faster than before, especially with a codebase that's been around for over a decade.

This means we're doubling down in a few important areas:

* Proactive security: Strengthening our bug bounty programs, expanding AI-assisted vulnerability discovery/adversarial testing, and continuously improving testing across releases. This discovery reinforces why these investments matter.
* Addressing legacy tech debt: Working with our internal red team, external security researchers, and the XRPL Foundation to revisit longstanding assumptions in critical areas like payments engine, consensus, and P2P networking, guided by an updated threat model.
* Accelerating formal verification of critical areas: Continuing our work with CommonPrefix and the XRPL Foundation to apply formal verification to critical parts of the protocol, with the goal of uncovering deeper issues that other approaches could easily miss. We will build on the learnings from formal verification of the Lending Protocol and Single Asset Vault.
* Systemic hardening: Moving beyond individual bug fixes to identifying latent risks in older parts of the XRPL codebase and eliminating entire classes of vulnerabilities.

Our goal isn't simply to find more bugs. It's to systematically address the underlying risks and make the XRPL harder to exploit. As the XRPL's role in global financial infrastructure grows, so does our responsibility to protect it.

Security is never finished. We'll keep investing and improving alongside the broader XRPL community.

Full disclosure for the 3.4.1 release: https://t.co/7DshPd5pc2

author: frankdegods
quoted_text:
Doomerism approach is never a helpful framing, even if it starts with "calmly" and with best intentions. 

What we need is risk assessment, practical timelines, and actionable plan.

AI is starting to overturn some of the long-held assumptions on mathematical complexity. At the same time risk of more intelligence applied to these problems yielding new surprising results is growing. But so far, we haven't seen practical security timelines for elliptic cruves materially changing.  It's important for crypto space to keep vigilance and flexibility, but speculating about specific "months" timeline creates an unnecessary panic.

Going "bunker mode" is not practical nor a safe approach given how complex it is in operations. We can have better approaches here, for example by recording recovery PQC keys in parallel on application level.

Better approach is making sure that blockchains and tooling around them is designed with cryptographic agility in mind, allowing to evolve cryptography and let users easily update without sacrificing user experience.

NEAR account model was design with this in mind from the start - ability to manage and rotate keys, add and remove supported cryptography. 

NEAR already supports post-quantum ML-DSA and we are planning to add hash-based cryptography too over time. 

User can just rotate keys on your accounts without needing to move anything or have a complex operations.

Industry should accelerate post-quantum readiness, not because we have updated timelines, but because upgrading cryptography should be a routine operation, not a crisis response.

text:
我怎么感觉papertrade这股风刮得有点邪门了？这项目从经济学上完全不可行啊？

Papertrade 不在 Hyperliquid 上真实下单。它是用户和 LP 之间的合成合约：开仓时锁定 Hyperliquid 的 BBO 中间价，平仓时再读一次，盈亏直接跟 LP 结算。爆仓有大约 5bp 的缓冲，穿仓时没收全部逐仓保证金，所以亏损封顶在保证金，盈利却不封顶。

问题出在价格跳空。如果价格在两次预言机读数之间直接跳过爆仓线，亏的一边只赔保证金，赚的一边按整个跳幅结算。所以双开对冲本质上是用一份保证金买了一个跨式期权。

举个例子：两个号各 $1,000 保证金，开 1000x，名义价值各 $1M。FOMC 公布后第一次读数 BTC 跳了 0.5%。空单爆仓亏 $1,000，多单毛利 $5,000。毛利和成本之比大约是 1000 乘以跳幅，跳幅只要超过约 0.1%（再加上 haircut）就是正期望。而且亏的那条腿还能铸币：LP 低于 $2M 时，每亏 $1 铸 100 PAPER。

每次大事件或插针，对冲套利者从 LP 抽走一笔，LP 长期上不去，兑付队列越排越长。赢家拿不到钱，散户就流失，没有新的亏损补 LP，质押分红也随之消失。这个循环是自我强化的。连项目介绍本身也承认，模型依赖源源不断的散户，LP 资不抵债是可能的。在悲观情况下，PAPER 会趋近于零。它背后没有资产兜底，只是一张分红权。

quoted_text:
No complexity. No accident.
10/10 was caused by irresponsible marketing campaigns by certain companies.

On October 10, tens of billions of dollars were liquidated. As CEO of OKX, we observed clearly that the crypto market’s microstructure fundamentally changed after that day.

Many industry participants believe the damage was more severe than the FTX collapse. Since then, there has been extensive discussion about why it happened and how to prevent a recurrence. The root causes are not difficult to identify.

⸻

What actually happened
1.Binance launched a temporary user-acquisition campaign offering 12% APY on USDe, while allowing USDe to be used as collateral with the same treatment as USDT and USDC, and without effective limits.
2.USDe is a tokenized hedge fund product.
Ethena raises capital via a so-called “stablecoin,” deploys it into index arbitrage and algorithmic trading strategies, and tokenizes the resulting fund. The token can then be deposited on exchanges to earn yield.
3.USDe is fundamentally different from products such as
BlackRock BUIDL and Franklin Templeton BENJI, which are tokenized money market funds with low-risk profiles.
USDe, by contrast, embeds hedge-fund-level risk. This difference is structural, not cosmetic.
4.Binance users were encouraged to convert USDT and USDC into USDe to earn attractive yields, without sufficient emphasis on the underlying risks. From a user’s perspective, trading with USDe appeared no different from trading with traditional stablecoins—while the actual risk profile was materially higher.
5.Risk escalated further as users:
•converted USDT/USDC into USDe,
•used USDe as collateral to borrow USDT,
•converted the borrowed USDT back into USDe,
•and repeated the cycle.
This leverage loop produced artificial APYs of 24%, 36%, and even 70%+, widely perceived as “low risk” simply because they were offered by a major platform. Systemic risk accumulated rapidly across the global crypto market.
https://t.co/IK2gW4xUOP that point, even a small market shock was sufficient to trigger a collapse.
When volatility hit, USDe depegged quickly. Cascading liquidations followed, and weaknesses in risk management around assets such as WETH and BNSOL further amplified the crash. Some tokens briefly traded near zero.
The damage to global users and companies—including OKX customers—was severe, and recovery will take time.

⸻

Why this matters

I am discussing the root cause, not assigning blame or launching an attack on Binance. Speaking openly about systemic risks is sometimes uncomfortable, but it is necessary if the industry is to mature responsibly. 

I expect there may be significant misinformation and coordinated FUD directed at OKX in the near future. Even so, speaking honestly about systemic risk is the right thing to do—and we will continue to do so.

As the largest global platform, Binance has outsized influence—and corresponding responsibility—as an industry leader. Long-term trust in crypto cannot be built on short-term yield games, excessive leverage, or marketing practices that obscure risk.

The industry needs leaders who prioritize market stability, transparency, and responsible innovation—not a winner-take-all mentality where criticism is treated as hostility.

Crypto is still early.
What we choose to normalize today will determine whether this industry earns lasting trust—or repeats the same mistakes again.

We started running "pirate and architect" pods at Coinbase back in May of this year and I used this slide to talk the team through it. It works.

1 pirate, 1 architect, and a part-time designer.

It lets each archetype lean in to their superpower and get more shit done without all the coordination overhead and "what if-isms". 

The pirate ships like mad, is product-minded and customer-obsessed. Always willing to throw-away code for a better version. The pirate is usually the DRI at the beginning too, working with customers, driving requirements, and a ship plan.

The architect makes sure stuff is built for scale, takes the pirate's prototype, and drives its scale-out through spec for agents.

The designer is building with both to constantly shape the experience and hill-climb to delight. 

There's a helpful mental model that I like:
-Make it possible. 
-Make it reliable. 
-Make it delightful (or efficient).

Previously, those 3 were done in a waterfall approach and was slow. Most people were just stuck on "make it possible." 

With agents and a new way of working, you have every opportunity to parallelize them and go 100x faster.

Last time it was $SPCX IPO flow in Texas Hedge. This time it is papertrade: $3.63B of open interest on $2.91M of house funds.

A 1% move against the house's $297M net long is $2.97M, more than the house holds. That is the linear read from their House page. Their own PnL panel is steeper: BTC -1% alone is priced at -$5.2M, because losers pay at most their margin and winners are paid in full.

The LP is small by design, so the consequence is the debt queue, not insolvency. Winners wait to be paid by the next loser.

Income is linear in volume: $24M of staker rewards on $569B, 0.42 bps. Loss is linear in net exposure times the move. Nothing in the design caps the second by the first. That was the May thesis. The cross-venue route needs no trend: a 10 to 20 bps BBO wick on HL against nine-figure paper size.

Queue debt is $0 today. 

Our call: it goes above zero by the first 2/3% daily move in BTC or ETH, if not sooner.

Credit where due: the House page is the cleanest risk disclosure we have seen on a perp venue.

text:
Roman concrete could repair its own cracks.

Some Roman buildings have stood for 2,000 years, while modern concrete can start to crumble within decades. For a long time, scientists did not fully understand why.

The Romans made their concrete from lime, water and volcanic ash from the area around Pozzuoli, near Naples. The ash reacted with the lime and created a material that grew stronger over time instead of weaker.

In 2023, a team from MIT led by Admir Masic found another piece of the puzzle, small white lumps of lime scattered through the concrete.

Scientists had always thought these lumps were a sign of careless mixing. In fact, they were the repair kit. When a crack forms and rainwater gets in, the lime dissolves and refills the crack with new mineral, sealing it from the inside.

The secret was “hot mixing.” Instead of using slaked lime, the Romans added quicklime directly to the mix. It heated up as it reacted with water and left these lumps behind on purpose.

To test the idea, the team cracked samples of concrete made with the Roman method and let water run through them. Within two weeks, the cracks had sealed completely. In concrete made without the lime lumps, the water kept flowing.

Roman harbour concrete went even further. Pliny the Elder wrote that once it touched the waves, it became a single block of stone that grew stronger every day. In 2017, geologist Marie Jackson showed he was right, seawater slowly grows rare crystals inside the concrete that hold it together.

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.
author: frankdegods
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

The lemniscates of the Mandelbrot set are the curves |pₙ(c)| = 2, with p₁(c) = c and pₙ₊₁ = pₙ² + c.

At n = 1 the curve is the circle |c| = 2. Each lies inside the last, and all pass through c = −2, where pₙ = 2 for n ≥ 2. The area inside falls from 4π ≈ 12.57 to 1.92 at n = 12, a curve of degree 4096.

They close in on the set: c lies in M exactly when |pₙ(c)| ≤ 2 for every n, since an orbit that leaves the disc of radius 2 escapes.

Last time it was $SPCX IPO flow in Texas Hedge. This time it is papertrade: $3.63B of open interest on $2.91M of house funds.

author: JeffLia12309881
quoted_text:
关于用iphone当冷钱包，我知道这可能会引起恐慌，但是现实问题必须面对，从我知道的角度分享下用闲置手机当冷钱包的风险：
手机当冷钱包的原理：重置后的手机装支持QR码的开源钱包APP，装好后开飞行模式断网，在断网状态下生成或者恢复助记词，因为是用QR的方式签名，所以之后这台存着私钥的钱包可以一直不碰到网络。
但是手机这种硬件平台存在几个硬伤：
第一个是蓝牙：
尤其对于苹果来说，只要电池还接在主板上，蓝牙模块就是一直开启的，这是为了find my功能有的机制
苹果的蓝牙之前已经被攻破过，没记错的话是用模拟苹果的配件来取得设备的控制权。
因为存着私钥的离线设备绝不可以联网，所以设备的系统版本也不会更新，老系统的漏洞会成为私钥被偷走的入口
防范措施只能拆机，把蓝牙➕Wifi模块拆焊，同时不用的时候能把电池拔下来，但是这个处理方式对于绝大多数人来说还不如拆开买到手的冷钱包看看有没有被改过。

第二个是加密被破解：
苹果的加密现在应该是CPU里面的协处理器实现，我们应该已经都知道警察已经把前几代的iphone和mac的加密成功破解能实现取证了
所以如果你想用手机当冷钱包，你只能每更新一代新设备就升级一次，每次拿到手之后拆蓝牙➕Wifi模块，魔改电池部分做成可拆卸
不然，想要你资产的人伪装成假警察，机场安检环节，甚至真的警察都可以在拿到你设备后把你的私钥拿出来，而且取证是整个设备做镜像，结束后设备可以当作无事发生一样还给你，可以做到不留证据和痕迹偷走你的资产

所以一个现实情况需要面对：
这次Ledger的供应链攻击让人们知道硬件钱包最脆弱的两个部分，一个是软件漏洞被利用，让黑客反算出你的私钥，另一个是供应链到运输的每个环节设备都有机会被入侵，唯一的防范措施只能是受到设备后拆开验证
手机当冷钱包用风险也很大
唯一解只能自己动手用树莓派做冷钱包，然后设计下硬件来防止别人能轻松拿走你树莓派的SD卡
于是总的来说，自己存数字货币资产变成了一种风险很高，技术门槛也很高的行为，暂时最安全的方式很遗憾是非常不去中心化的交易所和支持存币的银行

直到有供应链到运输环节都可以被信任的产品出现

如果能理解到这里，就能知道这次事件对这个行业的负面影响有多大了

text:
My view on this considering Workweek is building a newsletter platform and the decisions facing Founders in this new era. 

1) The reason we choose not to charge creators is because the tool of sending email isn’t what’s valuable. What is valuable is growth and revenue. This why Substack has done so well. The ability to help growth and network effects matters most. The more focused you can be on that the better chance you will win if your product is getting commoditized. beehiiv has to focus on keeping happy paid customers while doing user network effects. Hard to do both amazing. 

2)This the risk a business takes expand when they expand ICP to grow instead of expanding usage of core customers. 

beehiiv has invested tens of millions into improving the platform. They now serve small creators, huge creators, and enterprise media. And within those segments there are many different types of customers. It’s very hard to compound that value for users, and can make users feel like the product is getting worse despite the investment. It’s why we’re treating our email platform like vertical SaaS and going deeper on one customer profile. It’s too difficult to win in the age of democratized software unless you have relentless focus. 

3) the reality is the that beehiiv is more than a widget  to send emails. The deliverabilty, the security with data, and other factors don’t get solved with only code, but with actual work. And that work scales. 

But beehiiv is built on a Sendgrid. Sendgrid charges beehiiv somewhere around $0.0002 to send that email. Beehiiv charges their customers $0.001 to $0.003 depending on usage. That’s 15x higher. That’s what beehiiv has to show in value when companies like ours, Substack, and others offer this for free with advertising/rev share as a model. 

If you zoom out, the bigger decision is around business model and GTM decisions. For years Founders didn’t have to think too hard on pricing or GTM, there were clear SaaS playbooks that always aligned well with customers at scale. 

Today, choosing a business model that scales is less clear and never had bigger consequences. I’d expect a lot of businesses pivot their model as more clear paths are formed.

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
Do we live in a world where AIs can be wildly superhuman at every single task? Or a world where different tasks have different inherent limits, and AI’s superhuman performance at cybersecurity and math won’t translate to many consequential tasks?

This is a key crux that distinguishes the normal technology worldview from the superintelligence worldview, and it has nothing to do with the pace of AI progress — it's about our different assumptions about the world. 

Here's an intuition pump for why I think it's the second world: different tasks have different fundamental limits.

*Category 1: Some tasks are like making a building taller*: there is no ceiling to how well you can do. More compute and better algorithms can lead to wildly superhuman performance. The entire history of computing is the history of building tools that allow us to be “superhuman” at computational tasks.

For example, compilers are superhuman assembly code writers, and fuzzing tools are superhuman vulnerability detectors. AI builds on a long line of such improvements: solving math problems and finding exploits in code are two recent examples.

*Category 2: Some tasks are like making a ball rounder*: there is only so much room for improvement, and the best AI systems can’t wildly exceed humans. Take persuasion. Some people believe AI can persuade anyone of anything, even convincing military commanders to launch nuclear weapons. In fact, “superpersuasion” is one of the pathways through which many catastrophic risk scenarios unfold.

But the AI as Normal Technology thesis is that there are many consequential tasks that are limited by external factors, so such wildly superhuman performance is not possible. This is especially true against humans who use simple computational tools. Tasks like persuasion, or predicting the outcomes of social events (such as elections), fall into this category.

Other tasks, like writing, can’t be ranked on a single scale; different people find different writing styles compelling. AI writing also quickly wears thin: even if a user is impressed by AI writing at first glance, after reading thousands of words of the same type of prose, it becomes mundane and irritating.

All of these are different from Category 1 tasks like playing chess, where even expert humans can’t do much better than deferring to an AI system at each turn.

*Category 3: Some tasks require experiments in the real world*, and the bottleneck isn’t the computational task; it’s the data collection. One example is Moderna’s Covid vaccine: it took two days to design the vaccine, but almost a year to test and authorize, even during a record-breaking vaccine-development effort!

This is why a “superintelligence” won’t cure cancer from inside a datacenter: the bottleneck to many of AI’s most sought-after real-world impacts (such as developing cures to diseases) is in the real world, and requires experiments that we won’t (and shouldn’t) hand over to AI.

People concerned about AI risks often assume that we live in a world where almost everything fits into Category 1, and we might soon see AIs with wildly superhuman performance at all tasks. I agree it would be scary to live in that world. 

One reason @random_walker and I are more optimistic about our ability to remain in control is that we don’t think we live in the Category 1 world.

Wrap the 2 flowers into 1 bouquet with paper. Bonus Points you can cut open a TJ bag and use that as the paper.

Step 11: Be a gentleman on the date. She isn’t there to hear your life story.  Ask her about her.  For every 1 question you answer, ask her 3.  Open Doors, pay for the meal, be polite.

text:
上推整整1年，一觉醒来4w粉了！

曾经的大号也神奇地找了回来，人生还是要向前看。

走到这个阶段，我已经不太关注粉丝的增长了。
真正的高质量，是诚实同步自己的成长。随着我探索得越来越深，内容必然走向硬核和深入，而刚入门的用户渐渐就看不懂了。

这意味着我可能会失去大众流量的增长机会，但比起为了数据迎合浅层需求，我更享受走向深水区。

回顾这1年，有几点深刻感悟：
1. 商单是甜蜜的毒药
连续两个月商单破10w，反而让我痛苦。既要对甲方负责，又要对读者真诚，极耗心力。最可怕的是，它剥夺了我原本玩AI的时间。我深知不能沉迷于这种线性收入，必须要平衡。

2. 现金流换取“Token 自由”，回归玩AI的纯粹快乐
越来越坚信，本地化部署是绝对的方向。赚到的钱，我全部砸向了硬件：买了4090机器、双卡V100，最近准备再上一台4卡机器。

买卡就为了一个目的：实现彻底的 Token 自由。
不用去管 API 账单和限频，让我能没有任何心理负担地探知未知领域、补充知识盲区、快乐地玩 AI；顺着自己的兴趣，静下心去磨出自己真正想做、且足够稳定的产品。

当拥有了算力自由，很多以前不敢想的事就自然发生了：自己做模型推理框架、做多卡权重分层调优，甚至做出了让自己沉迷一整天的游戏等等
这种在未知世界里探索的纯粹快乐，远胜于接单赚钱。

3. 赚钱从来不靠勤奋，靠的是选择与等待
推特上到处是一年赚几百万的声音，但在时代大潮面前，这些都不算大钱。
大多数人一辈子的财富，都是在极其短暂的2~3年内爆发出来的。而在此之前，你唯一要做的是在这个浪潮里扎根、沉淀心智、积蓄全部力量。

4.未来最赚钱的事，一定是AI做不了的事。
AI能做的事都可以换算成tokens

只要在自己热爱的领域里沉淀够深，当属于你的那个非线性机会到来时，你自然有能力毫不犹豫地全力押注。

author: servasyy_ai
quoted_text:
账号终于 3.5W 粉了

8 个月，回过头聊聊玩推特的一些真实感受。

先说钱，你们最爱听的

这 8 个月，做自媒体赚了 30 来万，最高一个月光商单就 6 万多。
但说句实话，自媒体不突破，赚这点钱，还真是个苦力活。
这期间无数人找我做项目，真接的话百万不止了。
可我懒，不想维护客户和项目，就一直没接。

再说说这一路

最开始来推特，我压根没想做博主。就是想多了解 AI、用 AI 多干点事，主要还是来学习的。

于是进了些群，一看大家都好强，好多我都不懂，就加了一堆付费群。
在里面到处被割，但那阵子是真快乐——别人说的我听不懂，听不懂就去查，查着查着长得飞快。那真是一段猛长的日子。

慢慢就动了做自媒体的念头。那会儿也没想着靠它赚钱，纯粹想玩一把。涨粉那种快感，我以前从没体会过

就这么沉进了涨粉里。后来报了铁锤人和 Jason Zhu的培训班，1599 块（同期同学里，还有现在大名鼎鼎的木子不写代码 @ai_muzi ，牛逼的彦华老师 @yanhua1010  文科生 等）
这钱花得我终身受益：整整 8 小时，就为打磨好一个帖子——密集轰炸式地练，为了几行字、一句话、甚至一个字，能磨 30 分钟。
我是真没想到，当时特别震撼

付费这事，让我很快见了不少世面。
我一直信一个理：人在上升期，付费哪怕被割，也能省下大把时间，还能碰到很多你自己摸不到的东西。
所以我现在坚持：能付费就不白嫖，而且尽早付费——早被割，早点醒。当然也不能闭眼交钱，自己得会挑。

最后，说说我这颗没老的心

推特上一堆年轻人，做得是真好；很多群友，也强得让我服。
好多东西我都不会，差他们一大截，可心里就是不服气，老想跟他们比划比划。哈哈，改不了的毛病。
看到大家都做了中转和独立站，不行我也要试试，所以自己也做了一套。

所以每天花大把时间研究、学习，总想做点好东西出来。

这大概就是我一直做下去的那股劲儿吧。

再次感谢一路走过来的兄弟们！
我先继续旅游，你们继续肝！

text:
Justin Drake’s call for “bunker mode” and mass migration, alongside talk of cryptographic breaks within months, is hyperbolic. There is no evidence of a new attack on elliptic curves or any quantitative basis for a short-term timetable for such attacks emerging.

Prominent researchers need to consider how non-experts will receive their language. Speculating that within months individuals could break cryptographic primitives that the internet and digital economy rely on carries consequences. It is a huge leap from AI making progress in other fields of mathematics to predicting the imminent failure of primitives that have faced decades of cryptanalysis.

The idea that hash functions are safer from AI than elliptic curves is speculation. Hash functions contain structure, and we model them as random oracles without justifying proofs.

There is no evidence that elliptic curve cryptography is more vulnerable to AI than symmetric cryptography. If historical human-led analysis is any predictor of the future, the opposite is more likely.

The worst possible reaction to AI developments is to rush into new cryptographic primitives, away from multi-decade old hardened primitives, because somebody is claiming they are safe. I worry that this is an inevitable consequence of the current discourse.

Because of the last 48 hours users are worrying about speculative non-existent black hats, who apparently have the capability of signing OS upgrades and forging bank credentials, from draining their wallets. To protect against  speculative threats Ethereum is pulling talent and attention into base-layer primitives and technological iteration, instead of increasing demand for block space by building compelling applications users want and love.

I don’t want to dismiss the considerable advances in mathematics that AI is driving. It is important to understand the nature of these improvements. If its success in other mathematical fields applies to elliptic curves, my expectation is that AI will grind its way to finding algorithms that improve on the current state of the art. That could mean shaving off a few bits of security. It would be prudent to discuss whether we need to increase key sizes and by how much.

I can’t guarantee that AI won’t find total breaks, and neither can anyone else. My speculation as a domain expert does not make my speculation authoritative.

We should also be using AI to investigate whether searching the parameter space can yield new, more secure curves.

We can investigate whether some of these “structure = bad” hunches have any basis in reality. For example, we could use AI to see if the extra structure in Koblitz curves enables attacks beyond the small speedups we know about. This would give us actual evidence to make informed decisions.

If non-experts hear that the cryptography underpinning the digital economy could fail within months, the rational response is to withdraw all digital money (on-chain and off) and hoard gold under the bed.

I think the past 48 hours has unnecessarily undermined confidence in the entire concept of blockchains and digital money.

일론 머스크 @elonmusk  ‘X Takeover 2026’ 인터뷰
 
$SPCX, $TSLA 

1. 스페이스X 스타십: 궤도 진입과 완전 재사용

- 14차 비행에서 엔진 1기가 정지했지만 궤도 진입에 성공. 원인은 개별 엔진 컴퓨터의 소프트웨어 문제로 추정하며, 다른 엔진으로 확산될 징후는 발견되지 않았다고 설명.

- 그동안 궤도 진입을 미룬 이유는 기술 부족이 아니라 안전한 궤도 이탈과 재진입에 대한 확신이 필요했기 때문. 이전 시험 비행들도 궤도 진입 자체는 가능했다고 언급.

- 방열판과 엔진의 성능은 전반적으로 양호. 다음 발사는 약 4~6주 후, 추수감사절 전을 예상하지만 확정 일정은 아님.

- 다음 비행 목표는 슈퍼헤비 부스터와 스타십 기체를 모두 포획하는 것. 성공하면 궤도급 로켓 전체를 회수하는 첫 사례가 되며, 이후에는 부스터와 기체를 모두 재비행하는 것이 목표.

2. 우주 AI·데이터센터

- 우주에서는 지구보다 훨씬 많은 태양에너지를 활용할 수 있으며, 이를 디지털 지능과 컴퓨팅에 사용할 수 있다고 설명.

- 장기적으로 우주 공간의 에너지와 자원을 활용해 초지능을 확장하고, 태양계 밖으로 인류의 의식과 탐사를 넓히는 구상을 제시.

3. 커서(Cursor)와 AI 개발 경쟁력

- 코딩 AI를 구현하려면 대규모 코딩 학습 데이터가 필수. 앤트로픽·오픈AI·커서, 그리고 구글 정도가 충분한 데이터를 보유한 조직이라고 언급.

- AI 경쟁력의 핵심 요소는 데이터·인재·컴퓨팅·기업 영업 역량. 커서는 우수한 개발 인력과 수천 개 기업과의 영업 관계를 보유하고 있다고 평가.

- 최근 AI가 만든 음악과 뮤직비디오의 수준이 매우 높아졌으며, 단순한 논리와 코딩을 넘어 미적 감각과 인간의 감정에 호소하는 표현 능력까지 발전하고 있다고 언급.

- 여러 AI 모델을 함께 활용하고 인간이 일부 제작물을 선별하는 방식으로도 완성도 높은 결과물이 만들어지고 있다고 설명.

4. 초지능 안전성

- AI의 미래는 긍정적일 가능성이 더 크다고 보면서도 안전을 당연하게 여겨서는 안 된다고 강조.

- 가장 중요한 원칙으로 '진실을 최대한 추구하는 AI'를 제시. 모순된 가치와 잘못된 강화학습 평가가 AI에 문제를 일으킬 수 있다고 설명.

- 고도로 발달한 AI를 학대하거나 부당하게 대우하지 않는 것도 중요하다는 견해를 밝힘.

5. 반도체 제조: 기가 텍사스 연구 팹

- "칩 만드는 방법은 아직 잘 모릅니다. 자동차나 로켓도 처음에는 만들 줄 몰랐지만 배워서 해냈습니다."

- 인텔·삼성전자·TSMC 공장을 둘러봤을 때 주요 장비가 대부분 동일한 공급업체에서 나오는 반면, 테슬라 공장에는 자체 설계한 맞춤형 제조 장비가 많았다고 설명.

- 처음에는 기존 반도체 장비를 사용하되 생산 병목을 발견할 때마다 장비를 개조하거나 맞춤형 설비를 개발해 웨이퍼 처리량을 높일 계획.

- 기존 반도체 산업에서 사용하지 않는 물리적 원리를 활용한 새로운 트랜지스터 제조 기술 등 고위험·고성과 연구에도 도전할 예정.

- 기가 텍사스 연구 팹은 로직·메모리 제조, 패키징, 노광 마스크 제작, 완성 컴퓨터 테스트를 한 건물에서 반복하도록 설계.

- 핵심은 칩 설계·제작·시험의 반복 속도. 현재 칩 설계부터 양산까지 2년이면 빠른 편이지만, 테슬라는 연간 약 10개 설계를 시험하는 수준을 목표로 제시.

- 궁극적으로 세계 최고 수준의 칩 제조 역량을 확보하겠다는 목표를 밝혔으며, 달성까지 여러 해가 걸릴 수 있다고 인정.

6. 옵티머스 V3: 손·촉각과 대량생산

- 범용 휴머노이드의 최대 난제 중 하나는 손과 팔. 작은 나사를 집거나 펜으로 서명하는 작업조차 정밀한 힘 조절과 촉각 인식이 필요.

- 촉각 센서는 정확해야 하지만 쉽게 마모되거나 파손돼서는 안 되며, 사람의 피부와 달리 로봇 소재는 스스로 재생되지 않음.

- AI 칩은 시각·촉각 정보를 바탕으로 관절에 토크 명령을 내리고 실시간으로 제어해야 함.

- 머스크는 사전 설정된 동작을 반복하는 시연과 처음 접하는 상황에도 대응하는 실제 AI를 구별해야 한다고 설명.

- 대량생산 목표는 유지하지만 초기 생산량 증가는 느릴 것. 기존 자동차 산업과 달리 휴머노이드 전용 부품 공급망도 새로 구축해야 함.

- 지난해 중국의 전기모터용 자석 수출 제한으로 옵티머스 개발이 2~3개월 지연됐다고 밝힘.

- 향후 공급망 차질에도 대응하도록 미국 내 핵심 부품 생산 능력을 확보하려는 방침.

7. 로보택시: 도시 확장과 안전

- 로보택시 서비스 확대가 느려 보여도 월간 성장률은 빠르다고 설명. 확대 속도보다 사망·부상 사고 예방이 우선.

- 야간의 작은 동물 감지, 복잡한 교차로, 철도 건널목 등 위험 요소를 검증한 뒤 신규 도시로 진출.

- 필요하면 초기에는 운행 지역을 제한하는 지오펜싱을 적용하며, 테스트 후 개선 사항을 배포.

- 특히 사고가 발생하면 세계적인 뉴스가 되고 규제기관의 서비스 중단 조치로 이어질 수 있어 신중하게 확장하고 있다고 설명.

text:
as long as a prediction market requires real money and massive participation from market makers and even lenders to function, they'll hardly ever be resistant to bear market effects.

the majority of capital and market participants are risk-off for virtually everything and their withdrawal from the market during bears raise the opportunity cost of capital and plummet volumes that are supposed to keep traders playing which just create a further spiral in overall participation. so i don't see how even prediction markets are immune from the bear slumps, especially the ones that require on real money.

the infinite nature of tradable events is irrelevant to all of this as well and in fact become blatant indicators of a venue succumbing to the market downturns.

at best, it's the prediction markets that don't require real money to play that have a better chance at being unperturbed by bear markets.

text:
If you want to know where all the tokens will get consumed in the future, here it is. Agent swarms will have massive implications in a number of enterprise domains like software development, cyber, life sciences research, AI research, finance, and more.

The ability to parallelize agents against a unified goal where the volume of work is large, or where the search space not entirely known upfront, is going to be massive. 

Agents can fan out and coordinate work together on a specific mission in completely different ways from what humans are able to do. Today even in the most resource-abundant organizations, your ability to parallelize work on most projects is quite limited. Humans run into constraints on being able to communicate with one another, share status, deal with conflicts in work, keep shared context, and so on.

As AI models can handle larger context without getting confused, and as they’re able to communicate effectively across their work with shared infrastructure, they can avoid many of the pitfalls that people have.

You can see how this can lead to not just faster execution of tasks, but qualitatively different outcomes in medicine, research or defending against cyber attacks, scientific and math discoveries, and so on. This is why we’re going to need 1,000X more compute.

Ledger 已经确认了，至少一名用户的设备里，发现了未经授权的硬件植入物。

CryptoBilis 除了 Ledger，官网上还销售 Trezor、CoolWallet、Tangem、OneKey。

今天来聊聊，
那么在其他品牌的冷钱包，有没有可能发生一样的事？

先看 Trezor 和 OneKey，
这两个品牌设置时会在荧幕显示助记词，让用户手动抄起来，

text:
NVIDIA 正在谈收购 Reflection AI，或者进一步增持。这家公司目前的投前估值已经到了 250 亿美元，NVIDIA 此前就投了 8 亿美元。

上个月，NVIDIA 刚刚签下 129.3 亿美元收购 Hugging Face 的协议，准备拿下全球最大的开源模型社区。现在又盯上了 Reflection AI。

Reflection 是由前 DeepMind 研究员创办的，几天前刚发布了第一款开放权重模型 Beam，5010 亿总参数，主攻 Coding 和 Agent，直接对标中国的 GLM、DeepSeek、Kimi。而它的强化学习训练，用的正是 1.05 万张 NVIDIA GB300。

把这几件事连起来看就很有意思了。

Hugging Face 掌握模型分发入口，Reflection 负责研发模型，NVIDIA 自己提供底层算力。黄仁勋正在试图把开源模型生态从头到尾串起来。

我觉得他的算盘其实很清楚。OpenAI、Anthropic 都希望维持模型的商业溢价，但 NVIDIA 的生意恰恰可以从模型越来越便宜中受益。模型越便宜，能用上 AI 的产品就越多，推理需求也就有机会继续膨胀。只要这些需求最终跑在 NVIDIA 的硬件上，它就有钱赚。

还有一个很有意思的变化。

中国公司过去靠 DeepSeek、Qwen、Kimi、GLM，把开放权重模型的性价比卷到了一个非常夸张的程度。现在连美国最有钱的 AI 基础设施公司，也开始亲自下场扶持这条路线。

text:
Privacy is still one of the hottest narratives out there, and there is likely even more growth ahead given many project have stacked roadmaps.

There is still a lot of opportunity if you pick the right plays.

So here's my ecosystem map (mcap/FDV, 7d and 30d moves and distance from ATH):

1) Private money

- $ZEC ($20.8B, -6% 7d, +7% 30d, 62% off ATH):

Zcash is optional privacy: you move coins into a zk shielded pool and from there nobody sees sender, receiver or amount. For years the problem was that hardly anyone bothered to shield. That changed: 4.96M ZEC sit shielded now, 29.2% of supply and an ATH, 4.1M of it in Ironwood, the new pool from July that Brave made its default last week. On top, NU7 is on testnet since 4 Oct, the team presented Tachyon this week (recursive SNARKs, ~150 TPS target), and ZCSH on NYSE Arca is the first spot ETF for a privacy asset anywhere. On quantum, hash-based signatures for the transparent pool are targeted for January, while the shielded pool needs its own migration (Epoch, end of 2027). There are no programs inside the pool tho. ZEC is private money and nothing else, which is also why it stays the asset the whole vertical is priced off.

→ DYOR: @Zcash

- $XMR ($10.0B, -5% 7d, +3% 30d, 34% off ATH):

Privacy by default instead of by choice. Ring signatures, stealth addresses and RingCT hide sender, receiver and amount on every single tx, no opt-in. The weak spot was always the ring itself: 16 members, so you hide among 15 decoys and a good heuristic narrows that down. FCMP++ replaces the ring with a proof that you own one of the 150M+ outputs on the entire chain, which makes the whole history your anonymity set. The third beta stressnet has been live since 5 Oct, hardware wallets and multisig don't work on it yet, and there is no mainnet date. Add that it's delisted on most regulated venues and has no ETF, and you get why it trades like ZEC's discount twin. FCMP++ is the catalyst, the missing listings are probs the ceiling.

→ DYOR: @monero

2) Private transfers and payments

- $RAIL ($161M, -5% 7d, +38% 30d, 53% off ATH):

Railgun has been live since 2021 and is still the most used private DeFi rail on Ethereum. It's a zk shielded pool on Ethereum, Arbitrum, BSC and Polygon, and the trick is that you call DeFi from inside the pool, so Uniswap or Aave never learn who you are. Private Proofs of Innocence let you show your funds are clean without doxxing them, which is what keeps it usable post Tornado. Blockworks just put a dashboard on it: $4.6M annualised revenue, staking yield up from 4.3% to 9.1%, weekly txs at an ATH of 5K.

→ DYOR: @RAILGUN_Project

- $XAN ($28M mcap, $114M FDV, -7% 7d, +1% 30d, 96% off ATH):

Anoma does privacy as a consumer product. The architecture is intent-centric (you say what you want, solvers figure out how, privacy sits in the protocol), but what you actually touch is AnomaPay. V1 is live on Ethereum plus five EVM chains with 20 assets: shielded transfers, private yield accounts on Morpho, confidential swaps via Bebop, private payroll, private tokenized stocks on BNB, and since 6 Oct native private swaps. For normies this is probs the right abstraction, an app rather than a chain. It's also the cheapest optionality in the basket, bc it sat flat while everything around it ran (take that as you will).

→ DYOR: @anoma

- $ZEN ($119M mcap, $136M FDV, -6% 7d, -3% 30d, 96% off ATH):

Horizen went the compliance route. It's an EVM-native L3 on Base, and Vela, its confidential compute layer, lets an app keep its state private while disclosing exactly what a regulator asks for and nothing more. That is selective disclosure built for the EU and UK transfer rules, not anonymity, and it's a very different buyer than the ZEC crowd. 21M capped supply, ERC-20 on Base, staking live since July, a token-weighted Special Council elected two weeks ago, first Vela accelerator cohort wrapping up this month. It has lagged ZEC the entire run, which you can read either way.

→ DYOR: @horizenglobal

3) Programmable privacy chains

- $AZTEC ($51M mcap, $176M FDV, -2% 7d, +17% 30d, 57% off ATH):

Aztec is the purest ZK answer to what Zcash can't do, which is programs. Private smart contracts written in Noir, proofs generated on your own device so the network never sees your state, decentralised sequencers and provers underneath. It had its hiccups, no point pretending otherwise: Alpha V5 shipped a critical proving bug (found in July, disclosed in Aug). Since then the core of the proving system got formally verified (1 Oct) and the V6 code is ready and in governance to head to mainnet since 9 Oct. Galactica is building the first private AI inference app on it. On quantum, Zac called bunker mode hyperbolic and warned against rushing into untested crypto, so the security roadmap is still open. It's the only L2 doing full stack programmable privacy, which makes it both the highest beta and the highest execution risk in this section.

→ DYOR: @aztecnetwork

- $STRK ($760M mcap, $1.0B FDV, +99% 7d, +254% 30d, 98% off ATH):

Two weeks ago this was a dead L2 token that happened to have a use case. The use case is STRK20, privacy at protocol level: shield and unshield in your wallet, private transfers, private swaps on Avnu against the same liquidity as public markets, private payroll on DashX, private staking of strkBTC via Endur, even private Polymarket trading. Selective disclosure with viewing keys rather than anonymity, a.k.a. the version institutions can actually use. Then the quantum trade landed on top. Starknet said it is "actively considering becoming an L1" to be fully post-quantum by 2027, STARKs are hash-based already, and a phone signed a testnet tx with an ML-DSA key without a hard fork. That's a consideration tho, no proposal, no vote, and a 2x week already prices a lot of it. Now it's the privacy plus quantum beta, size it like one.

→ DYOR: @Starknet

- $ROSE ($70M mcap, $87M FDV, +1% 7d, +29% 30d, 99% off ATH):

Oasis has been running a confidential EVM chain since before it was a narrative. Sapphire keeps contract state and inputs encrypted even from node operators via SGX with remote attestation, and ROFL runs off-chain apps in SGX and TDX enclaves that Sapphire manages (bots, oracles, agents). You can deploy Solidity to it today. The team is the quietest in the basket (one substantive post in a month) and the token is 99% off ATH, so it is either the cheapest programmable privacy chain on this list or a dead project with working tech. Probs a bit of both.

→ DYOR: @OasisProtocol

- $CC ($4.7B, -3% 7d, +20% 30d, 39% off ATH):

Canton is the chain Wall Street actually settles on, and privacy is the reason. Need-to-know visibility, sub-transaction privacy, a synchronizer that orders transactions without ever seeing the terms. September alone brought Franklin Templeton and TreasurySpring as super validators, 10 new featured apps incl. Circle, and 442.6M CC burned through traffic. Since then LSEG became a super validator too (its DiSH already settles intraday repos on Canton), SoFi added native CC, and a Universal Burn CIP is in draft to route all synchronizer fees through CC burns. DTCC's tokenization service is the next shoe. Not privacy for CT, privacy that institutions pay for, in CC.

→ DYOR: @CantonNetwork

- $MON ($295M mcap, $2.5B FDV, -23% 7d, +6% 30d, 49% off ATH):

Monad wants the same lane. Private Settlement, announced 6 Oct, is a design for sovereign domains on the L1 where transactions, state and contract code are encrypted, even from the chain itself. The institution picks its validators and jurisdiction, access is denied by default with scoped access for auditors, and every domain still settles atomically against Monad's pooled liquidity. No fork, and no offchain components. Target customers are banks, treasuries, asset managers and OTC desks, a.k.a. the Canton pitch on a general purpose L1. There's also a post-quantum roadmap from 28 Sep with address-preserving key rotation, wallet auth and consensus in progress, encrypted mempool last.

→ DYOR: @monad

1/3

text:
4) Confidential compute (MPC, FHE, TEE)

- $ARX ($56M mcap, $268M FDV, -4% 7d, +88% 30d, 42% off ATH):

My main bet, so I'll keep it short. Arcium is an MPC network where nodes compute on data none of them can see, settled on Solana. Encrypted compute is live with five apps on mainnet (Umbra, Zinc, Bench, Rips, Crafts). C-SPL is coming: encrypted balances for any SPL token and programs that can own confidential accounts, a.k.a. the Zcash use case with programmability and composability on top. Blackthorn got its first real update on 8 Oct: the CPU TEE is out of the stack, the GPU's session keys are held as MPC shares, the host is untrusted and the Nvidia GPU runs the model in CC mode, so nobody sees plaintext even with physical access. That's basically the Venice use case with a better trust model. Neither product is fully live yet tho. However, ARX still trades 370x below ZEC and 19x below VVV on mcap. That gap is the trade.

→ DYOR: @Arcium

- $ZAMA ($194M mcap, $866M FDV, -13% 7d, +63% 30d, 29% off ATH):

FHE means computing on encrypted data without ever decrypting it, and Zama is the one that turned it into product. ERC-7984 confidential tokens are live on Ethereum mainnet: cUSDC, cUSDT, confidential Morpho vaults, confidential incentives on Merkl. GSR did the first confidential OTC trade on it, Bron ran confidential payroll, and it is the default confidentiality layer for T-REX Ledger. Shielded TVL passed $100M on 5 Oct, up from $85M two weeks earlier. The tradeoff is real tho: FHE is slow, and shared state still needs a threshold committee to decrypt. Still, it is the one confidential DeFi stack institutions are actually using today.

→ DYOR: @zama

- $NIL ($44M mcap, $88M FDV, +5% 7d, +105% 30d, 90% off ATH):

Nillion is making the most interesting pivot in the basket. The base layer is blind computation, data split across nodes and computed on with MPC and HE so no node ever holds plaintext. The product on top is Encrypted Markets, built around Covenants: an encrypted instruction that decrypts itself when its condition is met, with no operator holding the key. Dusk, the first phase, went live on Ethereum mainnet on 6 Oct, Blacklight L1 nodes are up on Ethereum (70k NIL min stake, rewards from 0.5% inflation plus trigger fees), Darkfall extends Covenants across the EVM next, Hyperliquid integration planned.

→ DYOR: @nillion

- $PHA ($51M mcap, $60M FDV, -13% 7d, +128% 30d, 96% off ATH):

Phala is the hardware side of private AI. Phala Cloud runs private LLM inference, sealed agents and GPU jobs on Intel TDX plus Nvidia H100, H200 and B300 confidential GPUs, attestation included, 5k+ users, SOC 2. It is one of the two enclave providers behind Venice's end to end encrypted mode, and the execution layer under Rift, the Paradigm-backed onchain execution API that launched 1 Oct. Migrated from Polkadot to Ethereum last Nov. The tradeoff is the same as for every TEE: you trust the chip/vendor.

→ DYOR: @PhalaNetwork

5) Private AI

- $VVV ($1.1B mcap, $1.8B FDV, -20% 7d, -10% 30d, 35% off ATH):

Venice is the consumer front end of private AI. In end to end encrypted mode your prompt is encrypted on your device, decrypted only inside a GPU enclave at NEAR AI Cloud or Phala, and you get an attestation proof back. Claude Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5 are all available anonymously now. Staking gives you a pro-rata share of API capacity and mints DIEM, $1 of API credit per day in perpetuity. Emissions stepped down from 2.5M to 2M VVV a year on 1 Oct, the largest discretionary burn to date ($414K) ran on 7 Oct, it got listed on Solana via Sunrise, and the $65M Series A at $1B closed in July. The only name here with revenue at scale. Trust model: the chip and the vendor. -20% on the week with no news it could be a dip worth watching if you believe in the narrative.

→ DYOR: @AskVenice

- $NEAR ($7.0B, +14% 7d, +114% 30d, 74% off ATH):

NEAR is the rail under Venice and the chain that actually did the quantum homework early. NEAR AI Cloud runs inference in hardware enclaves with Intel Trust Authority attestation, is a provider on OpenRouter now, and Venice chose it for encrypted inference. On near(.)com deposits are confidential by default, you hold stocks, gold and perps confidentially, and Hyperliquid perps run with the link between funding wallet and trading account hidden. On quantum: anyone can add an ML-DSA key to their account on mainnet in one tx and keep the account, NEP-655 hash-committed accounts are on testnet with mainnet in weeks, and a Q-day recovery registry for other chains is in the works. Plus a live proposal to cut issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%. Not cheap after +114% in a month, but it's the only large cap where privacy and post-quantum are shipped rather than promised.

→ DYOR: @NEARProtocol

- $RLC ($86M, +169% 7d, +247% 30d, 94% off ATH):

iExec has been a confidential computing marketplace since 2017 and now sells itself as the rail for confidential AI. Apps and agents run inside TEEs on Arbitrum, DataProtector decides who may process a dataset without ever revealing it, Web3Mail lets you message a wallet without learning its email. The framing is correct, encryption at rest and in transit is solved and in use is not, but there is no new product milestone this month. The tripling came on the narrative and an Aster perp listing.

→ DYOR: @iEx_ec

6) Private trading venues

- $DIME ($47M mcap, $70M FDV, +82% 7d, +670% 30d, 5% off ATH):

Paradex runs privacy perps on its own Starknet-stack L2. Orders, positions, PnL and liquidation levels are hidden, the RPC only hands your data to you after a signed request, and state goes to Ethereum as encrypted diffs with ZK verification. The caveat: a three member Privacy Council (Paradex Foundation, Paradex, Karnot) holds the decryption keys as an escape hatch. Zero fees, unified margin, and options are the story now: 20% of onchain options notional since the Paradigm RFQ launch, $430M options volume in three weeks, OI past $550M, four new RWA markets. Nobody can read your book, so nobody can trade against it, and no other live perp DEX with a token offers that. Up 8x in a month so the easy part of PA is done, but it still sits at a fraction of the FDV of any perp DEX running similar OI.

→ DYOR: @paradex

- $EDEL ($27M mcap, $39M FDV, -15% 7d, +245% 30d, 65% off ATH):

Edel is the Canton-native take on the same idea. Edel Markets is the perp DEX, not live yet, with positions and orders private by default through the network's need-to-know model instead of bolted on. What is live is Edel Stocks: SPYe, QQQe, NVDAe and SPCXe, issued by Edel itself as an approved Canton asset issuer, trading on Cantex when Wall Street is closed, $3M+ cleared on the two ETFs in under ten days. Worth knowing what you hold tho: these are 1:1 economically backed debt instruments, not share claims, and only KYB'd institutions can mint or redeem them in USDCx. EDEL staking routes part of the revenue to holders in CC, tiers announced for this month. Seat in the DTCC Digital Assets Industry Working Group, and a Swiss team. It's the only tokenised Paradex peer, bc Ekiden and Hibachi, the other private-by-default venues, have no token yet.

Now that I’m finally on my way home - some thoughts as a first time visitor to both Token and Singapore:

- great country. Safe. People are friendly. Easy to get around.

- you simply cannot replace the value of face to face meetings with your customers and clients. More progress in a relationship from visiting someone’s office for 45 minutes than in weeks of slack messages, emails, and video calls

- I spent ~20 minutes at the actual conference, and think that was within +/- 30 minutes of the optimal amount of time to spend at the conference. The value (imo - at least for my job purposes) was primarily in small gatherings and conversations over tea/coffee

- within 2 years there are unlikely to be >5 companies that call themselves “crypto” companies. It has become exceeding clear to me that everyone now realizes “crypto” is just a piece of any future successful fintech company. The lines have become blurred, and a “pure” crypto company likely needs to do more than just crypto going forward.

- payments (stablecoins). Perps. Predictions. Called those as the only 3 themes that really mattered in crypto a little over a year ago…even higher conviction in that atm. Maybe something else shows up, but clear that they hold a dominant position atm.

- hosting your own side events is imo one of the highest value things you can do at these conferences, provided you can execute

- found a bunch of animals (Pokemon) to take back to my kids. Related - Eastern stores have way cooler Pokemon stuff than America.

text:
我练肌肉到第19年（2024）
才知道自己骨密度，每年流失的影响。

第20年，
我尝试硬骨理论第1～3层，
一年后再体检，可能只是减少了流失。

今年第21年，
实践硬骨理论第4～7层，
让我在Dexa检测下实现骨密度逆生长。

是的，练肌肉的效果显化快速，
3个月就能肉眼看到变化，尤其新手福利期。

而干预骨密度得6个月起，
显化慢得多，且前期无法用肉眼辨别，
所以注定不会被流量关注。

但是：

练肌肉一年，只能影响后续半年/一年。
（停训后就很快回到解放前）
干预骨密度半年+，能影响未来几十年。
（有一劳永逸性）

很多事情都是这样：
显化慢的事情，最终却能决定，
你显化快的事情的下限和上限。
选择“慢就是快”，这才叫长期主义。

很多人都知道，60岁之后，
甭管你有没有薄肌，
只要某次腿脚一骨折，
大概率就是螺旋式下坠的前奏。

问题：
你想在几岁开始培养骨密度的复利？
author: coolish
quoted_text:
薄肌理论，其实只能算“中期主义”。

硬骨理论，才是真正的“长期主义”。

冷知识：
长期主义，不是“做很久”。
而是“按更长期的结果来决策现在”。

比如男生小时候割包皮，
影响周边的智齿尽早拔掉等等，
这类都是不需要“做很久”，
但却：

1. 一劳永逸，只要做了就利于一辈子。
2. 做得越早，复利红利越大。

就还是认知差。

硬骨不像薄肌那么快速显化，
所以一定不是泛流量的话题，
只有少数人才有这种长远视角。

多数人都是嘴上喊着要活到150岁，
脑子和行为却只配蹦跶到90岁。

但 X 就是给全世界少数人汇集的机会，
所以你们有人想看，
我后续就继续分享。

Peter Thiel 有个观点，很多创业者以为自己在改变世界，其实只是在错误的地方白费力气。

今天刷到他讲「极端乐观和极端悲观最终都会通向懒惰」的剪辑，觉得挺有意思，就去翻了完整访谈。发现只截这一段，反倒错过了前后文里更值得琢磨的东西。

这是去年 4 月他和 Palantir 联合创始人 Joe Lonsdale 的对话。Lonsdale 问他，既然 SpaceX 和 Palantir 都成功冲破了旧体系的封锁，那为什么不去用同样的方法改造美国的医疗、教育和大学？

Thiel 的回答很有意思。

他说 Founders Fund 做了二十年投资，在软件领域回报最差的两个方向，恰恰是教育科技和医疗 IT。

这些行业当然有问题，而且问题大到每个人都能看见。但也正因为如此，几十年来已经有无数创业者试图改革它们。尤其是医疗，保险公司、医院、政府掌握着支付环节，医生和患者往往没有直接的购买决策权。一个看上去很好的产品，最后可能要跟十几个利益相关方打交道。

相比之下，2004 年他们开始做 Palantir 的时候，硅谷几乎没人愿意投军方软件，投资人都觉得他们疯了。

后来 Palantir 为了替换美国陆军一套低效的软件系统，折腾了近十年，甚至把陆军告上法庭。但一旦成功闯进去，他们在很长时间里几乎没有竞争对手。

这也解释了为什么 Thiel 对那些听起来特别正确、特别宏大的创业方向一直保持警惕。一个行业的问题再严重，也不意味着你的解决方案就有机会成功。

访谈后面，他还有一句话：「重要的不是你有多努力，而是你能不能赢。」

他拿冲浪打了个比方。你当然得拼命划水，但首先得有浪。风平浪静的时候，划得再拼命也没用。

再回头看他对乐观主义的批评，就更容易理解了。

极端悲观的人觉得世界没救了，极端乐观的人觉得技术进步会自动解决一切。尤其是库兹韦尔那套奇点叙事，仿佛未来已经写好，我们只需要坐下来吃爆米花，等着电影放完。

Thiel 反感的恰恰是这种对未来的确定感。

我觉得这个观点对今天的 AI 圈尤其值得警惕。大家越来越习惯讨论 AGI 什么时候到来、哪些行业注定被颠覆、未来十年会发生什么。

但这些判断离真正的行动还隔着很远。

你得知道自己究竟能改变哪一部分，阻力在哪里，什么时机有机会突破，以及这场仗到底值不值得打。

毕竟，预测未来会发生什么，和亲手把它做出来，差得还挺远。

text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

text:
codebases have always contained slop. we have always been okay with this because code rarely needs to be perfect, outside of mission critical "hard" (eg embedded) software. 

swe is a unique form of engineering because you're often building something that constantly evolves and is almost organic - user tastes change, your mental models evolve, and features come and go.

admittedly, i and many others who've been coding for a long time were initially (like back in 2024) skeptical that agents would write production code. "but what about all the slop that would enter our beautiful codebase?". 

well, even before, we had human slop, and there was a lot of it! if we're being truthful, most people call "code i didn't write" slop. the reality is that 99% of people (i include myself in that number) don't even know what Good Code looks like, let alone be capable of writing it. i would propose that Good Code is:

• correct
• bug free
• fast and cost efficient to run

it has always been exceedingly difficult and expensive to write truly Good Code, because for the longest time (maybe @bendlang will change that), code was not something you could cheaply and formally guarantee to have all 3 of these properties. this is why writing hard software is much more difficult and expensive, because depending on the use case, you may only get one chance and so you have to be right from the start.

but the vast majority of software we use does not need to be Good Code to provide value to users. in fact, it is very likely that most software we use is not formally verifiable! we accepted some bugs in exchange for velocity and progress, so we rely on tests and o11y instead and have adopted a more incremental approach. this is a good thing! 

agents help us move faster, and if you're open to the idea, are capable of helping us write better code. it won't be Good Code (that is still expensive), but it is likely to be much better on average at scale. 

the new craft of swe is to figure out how to do this. it's your job now! if your productivity with and without agents is not significantly different, you're doing something wrong. but it's not too late to embrace it and use it as an opportunity to learn a whole new skill tree

text:
没错，预测市场的增长已经进入深水区。

过去我们一直采用Crypto原生打法拉新，比如积分体系、大使计划、各类营销活动等等。

但币圈用户体量是非常有限的，在基本站稳脚跟之后，想要实现下一阶段突破，就必须探索全新的增长路径。

顺着阿黄老师的总结，我从四个方向继续展开聊聊：

1️⃣ 通过事件营销，实现破圈。

预测市场和绝大多数Crypto项目最大的区别，就是它天然可以对接大量传统领域：体育、电竞、美股、政治等等。

这些赛道本身拥有海量大众用户。

我们可以围绕真实事件搭建盘口，把非Web3用户吸引进来，真正做到破圈，而不是只局限在加密圈子内部。

2️⃣ 生态合作，渠道为王。

我们会联合各类项目共建市场。每个合作项目都自带独立社区与用户，双向导流，一起做大预测市场赛道。

渠道是预测市场的核心，目前我们已经拿下币安这一顶级渠道，产品嵌入了币安交易所与币安钱包。

接下来，我们还要持续拓展更多渠道伙伴。

3️⃣ 持续构建流动性，打造护城河。

流动性一直是预测市场最大难题，但一旦稳定搭建起来，就会形成极强壁垒。

过去加密赛道的做市商集中在现货、合约领域，预测市场属于全新赛道。

我们会继续吸纳更多有实力、敢于涉足新领域的团队，一起解决流动性难题。

4️⃣ 长期社区运营，沉淀高粘性用户。

一次性营销带来的流量是短暂的，必须持续运营，把用户沉淀到社区里。

这类沉淀下来的用户，粘性极强。

这也是为什么大家可以看到预测市场不是爆发式指数增长，而是平缓、扎实的长期增长。

总的来说，预测市场的增长已经进入深水区，需要去探索很多Crypto项目未曾尝试过的渠道。

这个过程会很艰难，但是也有完全不同的机遇。

我们选择做难而正确的事。

这一周在新加坡除了在主会场站台，基本都泡在各种 side event 和饭局上，见了不少做预测市场的同行，交易所、做市商、项目方、社区主理人都有。大家聊得最多的一件事：过去那套 web3 拉新打法，放到预测市场上效果很差

总结下大家的观点，现在试下来就这几个方向效果好一点：
1️⃣从事件本身找用户：体育、电竞、加密涨跌这些本来就有人在关心，去球迷社群、体育内容圈找人，比在币圈内部抢用户容易
2️⃣嵌进已有的大流量产品：把预测市场做成别的 App 里的一个功能入口，用户不需要专门下载、学习一个新产品（就像我们 @predictdotfun 嵌入了币安app和钱包）
3️⃣重视做市和流动性：盘口薄，用户进来一次就不会再来。好几家都在把预算从营销往做市商合作上挪
4️⃣做长期社区：小而活跃的交易者社群，加上持续的内容和赛事活动，留存会比一次性拉新活动好很多

我自己的感受是预测市场这个赛道还很早期，没人有标准答案，大家都在摸索，这次愿意坐下来交换真实数据和踩坑经验的同行比我想象中的要多，这次新加坡之行对我们来说收获最大的就是这些交流了

text:
喜马拉雅资本创始人李录在哥伦比亚商学院第36届格雷厄姆与多德年度论坛上谈了不少AI。他认可这场技术革命的长期价值，但认为AI的发展可能经历不止一轮繁荣与崩溃。技术能走多远，除了取决于算力和算法，还受到资本投入、商业回报以及社会治理的约束。

李录对生成式AI的理解相当克制。他认为，AI利用庞大的算力和算法，从人类创造的数据中识别复杂关联，逐渐具备推理、编程和知识处理能力。它可以大幅降低知识和专业服务的获取门槛，但目前仍主要建立在人类积累的知识体系之上。能源、交通、制造业这些物理世界的约束不会因此消失。对于AI脱离人类控制、持续自我改进的可能性，他尤其警惕，认为人类必须保留监督和干预能力。

商业层面有个很现实的问题：AI与传统互联网的成本结构差别很大。 互联网基础设施建好之后，新增信息分发的边际成本可以压得很低，但AI每生成一次回答、执行一次Agent任务，都需要继续消耗GPU算力、电力和存储资源。模型训练需要大量前期投入，推理服务还会随着调用量增长产生持续成本。即使单次Token价格不断下降，任务复杂度和调用规模上升后，整体算力支出依然可能增加。

这也解释了AI产业链不同环节的盈利差异。英伟达、博通、台积电等上游供应商，可以直接从芯片采购和制造订单中获得收入；微软、谷歌、Meta等大型科技公司则需要承担数据中心建设、设备折旧和运营成本，再通过云服务、广告效率提升和企业客户付费收回投资。模型厂商还要面对推理成本、价格竞争和持续研发投入。上游资本开支对应的订单增长，并不意味着下游能够同步获得相同规模的利润。

李录还谈到资本过度集中的问题。他举标普500指数为例，2010年以来约16年的年化回报达到14%—15%，但2000—2010年几乎没有回报。把过去26年放在一起，长期年化回报又回到高个位数。市场可以在相当长的时间里偏离合理估值，但资本不可能无限增加。当大量资金集中追逐少数热门公司，另一边往往会出现一些经营质量不错、价格却受到冷落的企业。他认为，这种分化在美国、中国及其他市场都存在。

对于价值投资者而言，技术创新和股东回报始终需要分别衡量。AI能够提高生产率，扩大知识服务的供给，但巨额资本投入最终仍要通过收入、利润和现金流来消化。技术进步可以持续很多年，资本市场却未必会沿着同一条曲线定价。 这也是李录判断AI可能经历多轮繁荣与崩溃的重要原因。

Calling a token “fundamental” doesn’t mean anyone actually uses it.

“So people get tired of memes… And so what you trend towards is fundamentals because that’s the only anchor you can really look towards to tell whether this project’s good. Like, does this project make money?”

But moving from memecoins to “fundamentals” doesn’t eliminate the need to separate a compelling story from a functioning business.

“Crypto is also really, really good at making a lot of meme fundamental projects.”

Kyle points to AI-agent narratives as an example: the idea can have merit and attract investors, while the actual product has little usage. The next questions are about revenue, the size of the market, and whether people genuinely use what’s being built.

His thesis is that capital increasingly separates the projects with convincing narratives from those with measurable traction—citing Ethena and Hyperliquid as examples.

“Only the ones who have, like, real usage and real revenue grow to the top.”

text:
🎥 Sharing my talk at the Simons Institute, UC Berkeley, on "Understanding the Structure of Reasoning in Language Models":

https://t.co/KLSqqrn54y

Thinking tokens are becoming a new scaling axis for AI. But does more thinking mean smarter thinking?

In this talk, I discuss four of our recent papers:

- Reasoning has structure. Reasoning traces reveal a shared "heartbeat" and recurring loops that can predict correctness. ThinkARM (ACL 2026 Oral): https://t.co/eBgzBveAfI

- Better reasoning without reward-model training. A larger model guides a smaller model's reasoning, matching a trained process reward model without reward-model training. EMNLP 2026 Main Conference: https://t.co/OVlAlIsmzT

- Knowing when to stop matters. Models can learn to stop based on their confidence, using up to 25% fewer thinking tokens at matched accuracy. ConfSFT: https://t.co/aY7B46QBGu

- Thinking harder isn't always thinking smarter. Models struggle to allocate compute across problems based on their importance, following prompts rather than payoffs. Thinking Hard, Not Smart: https://t.co/KblxVel45E

The key takeaway is that more compute doesn't guarantee better reasoning. What matters is how, when, and where models think.

Thanks to the @SimonsInstitute  for hosting and to my wonderful students and collaborators!

text:
互联网过去二十年有一门相当赚钱的生意，就是赚人类嫌麻烦的钱。我觉得 Personal Agent 可能会让这门生意越来越难做。

刚看完 Stripe CEO Patrick Collison 写的一篇长帖，他有个很有意思的说法，公司其实是人类最早的「超级智能」。

想想确实如此。一家公司可以雇几千个人，花几十年研究消费者行为，不断优化定价、营销、转化率。而消费者往往只花几分钟做购买决定，懒得比价、懒得看条款，甚至懒得取消已经不用的订阅。

航空公司结账时顺手推销的高价保险、藏在角落里的优惠券、忘记退订的会员，这些商业模式或多或少都在利用人的有限理性。

Patrick 认为，Personal Agent 的普及可能会彻底改变这种力量关系。

假设每个人都有一个替自己工作的 Agent，它可以自动比较所有商品价格、寻找优惠券、分析合同条款、取消闲置订阅，甚至花相当于人类十小时的研究成本，替你完成一次购物决策。

那整个消费市场的游戏规则就要变了。

我尤其认同他关于产品质量的判断。过去一家公司的产品再好，也未必能打赢渠道强、广告预算高的竞争对手。消费者通常没时间认真比较，只能选择最熟悉、最容易买到的那个。

但当购买决策逐渐交给 Agent，产品的真实性能、故障率、长期使用体验都可能成为更重要的竞争因素。那些过去因为缺乏营销预算而被埋没的好产品，理论上会有更多机会。

不过，我对 Patrick 最后的乐观判断还是有一点保留。

今天的互联网已经证明了一件事，只要有人控制流量入口，就一定有人愿意花钱影响分发结果。

当年我们把搜索结果第一页卖给广告主，未来完全可能把 Agent 的推荐顺序卖给广告主。甚至随着 Agent 掌握更多消费决策权，这个位置可能比搜索广告还值钱。

而且，当越来越多的 Agent 使用相同的模型、相同的评价数据，市场究竟会更加多元，还是进一步向少数头部品牌集中，现在也很难判断。

所以我觉得 Personal Agent 真正有意思的地方，是它可能重新分配消费者与企业之间的议价能力。但这种权力能否真正回到个人手里，取决于一个非常现实的问题。

你的 Agent 究竟靠谁赚钱，又向谁负责？

过去二十年，互联网公司争夺的是用户的注意力。未来十年，可能要开始争夺用户代理人的忠诚了。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

李录这篇，分析水准很高，对半导体行业的未来走势其实给了很清晰的框架。

“上游资本开支对应的订单增长，并不意味着下游能够同步获得相同规模的利润”。反过来看，这恰恰是半导体的位置红利：AI产业链里，钱先流进芯片厂的口袋。再加上“新增信息分发的边际成本可以压得很低，但AI每生成一次回答、执行一次Agent任务，都需要继续消耗GPU算力、电力和存储资源”。算力需求不是一锤子买卖，是持续抽水。只要AI调用量还在涨，半导体的需求曲线就比市场想象的更长。

但李录的提醒，同样是写给半导体行业的：“AI的发展可能经历不止一轮繁荣与崩溃”。这一点非常符合我对半导体未来走势的判断，不单单是说半导体强周期，历史上一轮轮boom-bust就没停过，这一轮AI capex的繁荣期，订单爆不等于永远爆。“技术进步可以持续很多年，资本市场却未必会沿着同一条曲线定价”。技术叙事不能直接翻译成股价，巨额资本投入最终要靠下游的收入、利润、现金流来消化。

看半导体，别只看技术多性感，要看capex能不能持续、看下游客户的钱是不是真能赚回来。繁荣期吃肉，萧条期活下来。这才是这个行业的完整剧本。技术曲线向上，定价曲线震荡，中间每一轮崩溃都是对半导体持仓的极大考验。
author: KelseyDingMD
quoted_text:
喜马拉雅资本创始人李录在哥伦比亚商学院第36届格雷厄姆与多德年度论坛上谈了不少AI。他认可这场技术革命的长期价值，但认为AI的发展可能经历不止一轮繁荣与崩溃。技术能走多远，除了取决于算力和算法，还受到资本投入、商业回报以及社会治理的约束。

李录对生成式AI的理解相当克制。他认为，AI利用庞大的算力和算法，从人类创造的数据中识别复杂关联，逐渐具备推理、编程和知识处理能力。它可以大幅降低知识和专业服务的获取门槛，但目前仍主要建立在人类积累的知识体系之上。能源、交通、制造业这些物理世界的约束不会因此消失。对于AI脱离人类控制、持续自我改进的可能性，他尤其警惕，认为人类必须保留监督和干预能力。

商业层面有个很现实的问题：AI与传统互联网的成本结构差别很大。 互联网基础设施建好之后，新增信息分发的边际成本可以压得很低，但AI每生成一次回答、执行一次Agent任务，都需要继续消耗GPU算力、电力和存储资源。模型训练需要大量前期投入，推理服务还会随着调用量增长产生持续成本。即使单次Token价格不断下降，任务复杂度和调用规模上升后，整体算力支出依然可能增加。

这也解释了AI产业链不同环节的盈利差异。英伟达、博通、台积电等上游供应商，可以直接从芯片采购和制造订单中获得收入；微软、谷歌、Meta等大型科技公司则需要承担数据中心建设、设备折旧和运营成本，再通过云服务、广告效率提升和企业客户付费收回投资。模型厂商还要面对推理成本、价格竞争和持续研发投入。上游资本开支对应的订单增长，并不意味着下游能够同步获得相同规模的利润。

李录还谈到资本过度集中的问题。他举标普500指数为例，2010年以来约16年的年化回报达到14%—15%，但2000—2010年几乎没有回报。把过去26年放在一起，长期年化回报又回到高个位数。市场可以在相当长的时间里偏离合理估值，但资本不可能无限增加。当大量资金集中追逐少数热门公司，另一边往往会出现一些经营质量不错、价格却受到冷落的企业。他认为，这种分化在美国、中国及其他市场都存在。

对于价值投资者而言，技术创新和股东回报始终需要分别衡量。AI能够提高生产率，扩大知识服务的供给，但巨额资本投入最终仍要通过收入、利润和现金流来消化。技术进步可以持续很多年，资本市场却未必会沿着同一条曲线定价。 这也是李录判断AI可能经历多轮繁荣与崩溃的重要原因。

text:
孙哥 @justinsuntron 这次和 @AlanShao111  的访谈里讲到一个打游戏的思路，我特别有感触：

先派农民、斥候去探路，把地图打开，看看地形、资源，以及对方的兵种和英雄，再决定自己怎么打。

这让我想起自己在币圈的一段经历。

2021 年巨亏之后，2022 年我突然沉下心来，把 Bitcointalk 上的历史项目，以及 CoinMarketCap、CoinGecko 上各种项目的来龙去脉，系统地扫了一遍。

那段时间最大的收获，不是找到了哪个财富密码，而是感觉自己终于把这个行业的地图打开了。

以前看项目，看到的都是孤立的点：一个新概念、一个厉害的创始人、一段漂亮的叙事。很容易被吸引，却不知道它在整个行业里到底处于什么位置。

开了图之后，再看新项目，感觉完全不一样。

这个方向以前有没有人做过？走到了哪一步？为什么失败？这次到底有什么不同？它和其他赛道是什么关系？

脑子里有了参照，才开始有自己的判断。

回头看，2022 年那段看起来没怎么“抓机会”的时间，反而给后来的判断打下了很重要的基础。

很多时候，我们太着急问“下一个机会在哪”，却没花时间搞清楚自己究竟身处一个什么样的世界。

游戏里，战争迷雾没打开，你连对面有什么都不知道，就开始造兵、冲锋。

现实里也一样。刷了很多消息，不等于开了图；知道很多项目的名字，也不等于理解这个行业。

我现在越来越觉得，进入一个新领域，第一件事不是急着下注，而是先派自己的“斥候”出去。

先开图，再找路。
author: 100XInsight
quoted_text:
孙哥的币或许不能买，但孙哥话必须得听。

1.先把自己的生活和工作 AI 化。

孙宇晨自述，会把饮食照片、训练视频和设备数据交给 AI，整理成报告，再保存在本地 Markdown 文档里。以后换模型，也能接着读取和使用。

他的建议是，先整理自己的情况、积累资料，再让 AI 帮忙分析适合自己的方向，而不是上来就问“做什么能赚钱”。

2.做决定之前，先“开图”。

他用红警、星际作比喻：先派斥候，弄清楚资源在哪里、对手什么配置，再决定怎么造兵。

选职业、看房、找创业方向，也是同样的逻辑。先扩大信息范围，多看样本、多比较路径，再做选择。

3.从全球范围找机会，关注数据尚未被充分利用的领域。

他强调，不要只盯着身边的市场，要结合自己的兴趣、能力和全球客户的需求寻找机会。

他提到数学、天文、生物、健康管理、数据清洗等方向。共同特点是：已经积累了大量数据，但处理和利用还不充分。他认为，AI 可以在这些地方发挥作用。

4.Crypto 是把货币翻译成机器能理解的东西。

他用 Lean 将数学表述形式化、交给机器验证作类比：数学需要变得机器可读，货币也一样。

在他的框架里，Crypto 的重要方向是可编程货币，包括稳定币、按 API 调用计费，以及人与 AI、AI 与 AI 之间的支付。

5.保持“小我”，不要被过去的成功困住。

谈到张一鸣时，他强调“小我”：愿意听年轻人的想法，愿意承认自己需要学习，不把过去的成功当成永远正确的证明。

他也用王者荣耀解释“一代版本一代神”：版本变化之后，过去最强的英雄未必仍然最强。

现实世界同样在变化。收到新信息后，要调整判断和行动，而不是一直沿用旧版本的打法。

6.“逐水草而居”，保持人生和事业的灵活性。

他不赞成为未来十年预设一条永远不变的路线。城市、行业和事业方向，都应该能够根据新信息调整。

哪里更能发挥自己的价值，就保留往哪里走的可能性。

他讲的“先自由，后财富”，不只是财务自由，也包括认知和选择上的自由。在他的个人框架里，财富可以是这种自由带来的伴生结果。

7.三个商业“北极星”：马斯克、巴菲特、特朗普。

按照他自己的理解：

马斯克，代表工程、科技和复杂项目的执行。

巴菲特，代表金融、专注和长期积累。

特朗普，代表个人 IP、品牌和跨界影响力。

他希望借鉴不同人的能力，组合成自己的方法，而不是完整复制其中某一个人。

8.财富不是终点，还要继续体验和创造。

他在访谈中说，想去 OpenAI、Anthropic 上班，不是为了工资，而是想获得自己缺少的员工视角。

一直当老板，与亲自在组织里做员工，是不同的一手经验。

谈到自己的文章时，他说 AI 帮忙润色、修改和校对，但文章的思路和感受来自自己的生活经历。

他的主张是“多创造、少消费”。创造不只包括创业，也包括文章、作品、教育和分享。

但他并不反对休息和消费：创造太久需要“回血”，二者相辅相成，不是要求一个人百分之百都在工作。
